paper_core_claims.claim: A linear possibilistic-probabilistic optimization problem with possibility or necessity constraints, LR fuzzy-random coefficients and weakest-t-norm dependence can be reduced to a stochastic programming analogue with center and spread terms.

The equivalent convex stochastic program can be attacked by a projected primal-dual stochastic quasigradient method using sample-based estimates instead of exactly computing expected spread functions.

For continuous convex objectives/constraints, a convex closed decision set, Slater feasibility, diminishing non-summable square-summable steps and the stated moment/normalization controls, an accumulation point belongs to the solution set almost surely.

Assuming finite second moments for the random scale variables is presented as a more easily checked sufficient condition for finite conditional squared quasigradient norms and a simplified almost-sure convergence theorem.

function_concept_used_by_paper: The paper uses functions in the mathematical-optimization sense, not software functions or probabilistic-program terms. A decision vector x is evaluated by linear fuzzy-random objective and constraint functions f_i(x, omega, gamma); expected LR center/spread functions are transformed into a stochastic Lagrangian; sampled quasigradient functions drive a projected primal-dual iteration.
representation_or_carrier: The carrier combines a probability space (Omega, B, P), a possibility space (Gamma, powerset(Gamma), pi), real decision vectors in a nonnegative subset X, and fuzzy random variables Y(omega,gamma). Coefficients have a shift-scale representation a(omega)+sigma(omega)Z(gamma), with Z an LR-type fuzzy quantity represented by left/right core and spread parameters. Possibilistic dependence is specified by a t-norm, specialized to the weakest t-norm T_W.
specification_language: A constrained mathematical program specifies an extremized auxiliary/objective value, possibility or necessity thresholds tau_i{E[f_i] relation_i k_i} >= alpha_i, and x in X. Linear fuzzy-random functions, LR shape functions L/R, expectation, independence, weakest-t-norm relatedness and convexity/Slater/moment/step-size assumptions complete the model. This is not a programming language and has no types, modules, pre/postconditions, executable syntax, API, provenance schema or general function contract.
compiler_or_generator: No compiler or generator is presented. The reduction from the hybrid possibilistic-probabilistic program to equations 3-4 is a hand-derived mathematical equivalence under a narrow linear LR/weakest-t-norm model. No automatic translator, symbolic checker or construction algorithm is implemented, and the paper does not measure the cost of forming or solving the analogue.
interpreter_or_runtime: The runtime analogue is an iterative projected stochastic quasigradient primal-dual optimizer: sample omega^s, construct xi^s and zeta^s for the Lagrangian, update x by projected descent and u by projected ascent with step rho_s gamma_s. The paper supplies formulas and convergence conditions but no code, pseudocode with stopping rules, parameter-selection procedure, numerical example, benchmark or executable artifact.
composition_rule: Expected values combine probabilistic randomness with LR fuzzy parameters, and t-norms aggregate possibilistic dependence. The Lagrangian composes one objective with multiplier-weighted constraints, while vector quasigradients sum the corresponding sample contributions. This is algebraic aggregation for one constrained optimization problem; the paper does not define compositional semantics for independently deployable stochastic functions or prove closure under general program/function composition.
state_or_effect_model: Iteration state is the primal-dual pair (x^s,u^s) plus its filtration/history B_s. Fresh sampled scale realizations determine stochastic quasigradients, and projections keep updates in X and U. No mutable software heap, event trace, concurrency, nondeterministic control flow, external I/O, checkpoint/restart or distributed state is modeled.
uncertainty_model: Aleatory uncertainty is represented by P over omega and possibilistic/fuzzy uncertainty by pi over gamma. A fuzzy random variable couples both; LR membership/possibility shapes and t-relatedness describe fuzziness and dependence, while expectation removes omega to produce a deterministic fuzzy expected value. The optimization constraints use possibility or necessity levels alpha. The method assumes known distributions/moments and does not estimate, calibrate or update them; it reports no finite-sample confidence bound, posterior, robustness analysis or sensitivity study.

paper_core_claims.claim: Church is a dynamically typed applicative-order stochastic Lisp in which pure Lisp is deterministic, elementary random procedures introduce sampling, first-class expressions compose generative processes, eval samples them and query denotes conditional sampling.

Admissible expressions, including expressions with stochastic memoization, induce probability distributions over equivalence classes of evaluation histories and hence return values; positive-probability predicates give well-defined conditional query distributions.
Stochastic mem shares sampled generative history across calls, provides persistent random-world structure and can express Dirichlet-process memoization and several nonparametric models compactly.
Exact rejection and collapsed rejection implement query in principle, while a Metropolis-Hastings algorithm over computation traces is proposed for approximate conditional inference.

A single higher-order language can express causal Bayes-style models, infinite mixture/relational models, stochastic transition grammars and planning by inference without model-specific inference code.

function_concept_used_by_paper: A Church expression is a first-class higher-order stochastic function/program describing a generative process. Ordinary procedures close over an environment; elementary random procedures additionally expose a conditional probability function; eval turns expressions into samples; query conditions their induced history/value distribution; mem converts an admissible procedure into a persistent random function; and nested eval/query lets programs manipulate or reason about programs.
representation_or_carrier: Syntax and Scheme-like values are countable; real numbers are fixed/floating approximations. A procedure is body, arguments and environment, with elementary random procedures adding a distribution function. The semantic carrier is an evaluation history and its product probability; admissible expressions have total finite-history weight one and induce a value distribution mu(e,env). With mem, histories are quotiented by unused memo-table values. Approximate runtime state is a computation-trace DAG containing an evaluation tree, environment-extension tree and binding dependencies.
specification_language: Church provides dynamically typed Lisp syntax for constants, variables, application, lambda, if, define and quote; a standard library supplies higher-order operations and elementary random procedures; eval/query/lex-query specify generative and conditional computation; mem/DPmem specify persistent and exchangeable random functions. It does not statically specify types, support, admissibility, termination, evidence positivity, resource bounds, inference accuracy, convergence diagnostics, privacy, deployment or lifecycle policy, and the paper gives no machine-checkable contract language.
compiler_or_generator: No compiler or ahead-of-time generator is presented. The paper gives an informal interpreter definition and suggests future program analyses that might transform query into eval for exact enumeration. Because expressions are values, Church can describe priors over programs and program induction, but this is a representational possibility rather than an implemented or verified synthesis compiler.
interpreter_or_runtime: A prototype implements Scheme-like eval, finite memo tables and query. Exact recursive rejection is definable metacircularly but can be nonterminating or intractable; collapsed rejection marginalizes predicate randomness. Approximate query uses Metropolis-Hastings proposals over evaluation-history traces, repairing dependent evaluations and applying proposal corrections. At publication the MCMC implementation omitted mem, did not fully handle nested queries, omitted delicate trace-update equations for space and was explicitly too inefficient for typical machine-learning applications.
composition_rule: Lambda abstraction/application and higher-order functions compose deterministic and stochastic procedures; lexical environments route bindings; eval recursively composes sampling histories; query conditions the composed history distribution; mem shares results by procedure/argument; DPmem composes a Dirichlet-process cache; nested eval/query composes inference and program interpretation. Composition does not ensure admissibility, positive evidence, efficient inference, good mixing or bounded memory.
state_or_effect_model: Random primitive calls are probabilistic effects recorded in evaluation histories. Memoization creates persistent per-argument random state and supports random worlds; query conditions effects; recursion may diverge; approximate inference mutates a trace proposal. The denotational language is intended to preserve exchangeability/purity, while its finite implementation necessarily uses mutable association lists. General mutable state, concurrency, distributed execution, I/O failure, checkpointing and durable provenance are outside scope.
uncertainty_model: Uncertainty is a probability distribution over finite evaluation histories and marginal return values; conditional uncertainty is defined by query when the expression/predicate are admissible and the predicate has positive probability. Memoized random functions share latent variables; DPmem supplies nonparametric uncertainty; approximate MCMC adds algorithmic error. The paper gives no finite-sample error bound, posterior calibration, mixing theorem, ESS, acceptance-rate report, confidence interval or systematic comparison with ground truth.

equivalence_notions.boundary: The paper sketches the measure construction and gives no executable equivalence checker.
Syntactically distinct programs can agree distributionally, but no general decision procedure is supplied.
Undefined for inadmissible expressions and requires the conditioning event to have positive probability.
Trace repair details are omitted, nested-query support is incomplete and the MCMC implementation did not yet support mem.
No convergence/mixing proof or quantitative target-agreement experiment is supplied for the proposed MCMC implementation.

lifecycle_and_provenance: The 2008 paper is preserved by the official UAI site and a 2024 PMLR reissue with byte-identical PDFs, plus a separately hash-bound arXiv minor-corrections version. The provisional resolver instead captured an unrelated 2016 textbook homepage; its exact hash is reproducible only over HTTP because the current HTTPS hostname certificate does not validate. The paper cites a Blaise-based prototype and thesis but supplies no source URL, release tag, build instructions, dependency/runtime lock, test corpus, random seeds, trace archive, CI, security policy, compatibility matrix, revalidation cadence, rollback or retirement record. Later Church/WebChurch systems are not evidence that this specific 2008 artifact was reproducible as published.
limitations_and_failure_boundaries: The universal-language claim is about expressive computability/generative description, not guaranteed termination, normalized probability, efficient inference or practical learnability.
Only admissible expressions with total finite-history weight one define value distributions; recursion/fix can be inadmissible, and no admissibility checker is provided.
Query is undefined if the expression or predicate is inadmissible or if no supported value makes the predicate true with non-zero probability.
Recursive rejection query may not terminate for impossible evidence and is expected to be intractable for many low-probability events.
Countable primitive types and fixed/floating representations bound the language's numeric model; continuous distributions are runtime primitives rather than a measure-theoretic language proof here.
Formal semantic results are proof sketches, including the countably infinite memoized environment and quotient over histories; they are not mechanized.
Stochastic memoization can imply infinitely many latent values denotationally; the finite runtime creates entries lazily and can grow without a resource bound.
Exchangeability is proposed as stochastic purity, but general stateful extensions and their semantic conditions are explicitly future work.
The prototype MCMC algorithm had not implemented programs using mem, despite mem being a central language feature.
Nested-query handling is acknowledged as incomplete, and delicate trace-consistency/proposal corrections are omitted from the paper.
The MCMC section gives no stationarity, irreducibility, convergence-rate, mixing, variance or finite-sample correctness theorem.
Figure 9 is one 100-sample sprinkler run with 30 MCMC steps per sample, not a reproducibility or convergence study; no exact target or uncertainty band is shown.
Figures 6-7 are illustrative qualitative outputs with tiny synthetic setups, not empirical validation across tasks or comparison to baselines.
The authors explicitly state that the implementation is not efficient enough for typical machine-learning applications.
No runnable paper artifact, code receipt, seeds, environment, datasets, tests or trace logs accompany the source.
The registered probmods URL is an unrelated textbook landing page and its HTTPS certificate currently fails hostname validation, demonstrating weak source-registry lifecycle hygiene.
The paper does not connect Church semantics to neural weights, governed Function OS assets, ignition epsilon, frozen Psi_0 or production deployment.
what_the_paper_does_not_support: It does not prove that all Church programs terminate, normalize or admit well-defined conditional queries.
It does not provide complete or efficient generic inference for programs using mem, nested queries or rare/impossible evidence.
It does not provide an automatic equivalence checker, compiler, convergence-certified MCMC runtime or current reproducible release.
It does not establish quantitative superiority across Bayesian networks, nonparametric models, grammars or planning tasks.
It does not empirically validate neural function composition, artifact lifecycle governance, a probability law for ignition epsilon or ignition itself.

paper_core_claims.claim: Pyro is a Python-embedded probabilistic programming library on PyTorch that combines arbitrary Python control flow with GPU tensors and automatic differentiation.
A small core of sample and param primitives plus composable Poutine effect handlers separates model, inference and runtime behavior while allowing generic SVI, HMC and NUTS.
Pyro's model-guide interface permits learned approximate posterior programs while aligning unconstrained latent sample sites and their shapes.
The released system is open source, documented, tested and developed with continuous integration around a PyTorch backend.
Two publication experiments report moderate Pyro overhead relative to handwritten PyTorch VAE updates and DMM test ELBOs close to or better than a cited reference implementation.

function_concept_used_by_paper: A Pyro probabilistic function is an ordinary Python callable whose execution contains named sample, observation and parameter sites. Models specify joint distributions and guides specify approximate posteriors; inference algorithms invoke and transform those functions through Poutine handlers. The word universal refers to host-language expressive power over computable distributions, not a proved total or tractably inferable Function OS contract.
representation_or_carrier: The static carrier is Python/PyTorch source plus modules, tensors and named distributions. At runtime, each primitive constructs a message containing site name, distribution/function, arguments, observed value, inference metadata, scale, mask and conditional-independence stack. A global Poutine stack routes messages through messengers; trace records sample/param/module/subsample sites, values, shapes and dependencies; the global parameter store holds mutable named tensors.
specification_language: Python functions specify model and guide programs. pyro.sample declares a named random/observed site, pyro.param a learnable constrained value, pyro.module registers neural parameters, and plate declares conditionally independent replicated structure with optional subsampling. The model and guide share arguments; publication-near runtime checks compare latent-site coverage, auxiliary/enumerated sites, event dimensions, shapes and plate nesting. This remains a dynamic convention rather than a closed static contract: support, normalization, termination, conditional independence, approximation quality, effects outside Pyro, privacy, resources and lifecycle policy are not generally specified or proved.
compiler_or_generator: No general compiler or function generator is presented. PyTorch automatic differentiation and optional JIT-compiled ELBO evaluation optimize tensor kernels/gradients, while SVI constructs an optimization objective from model and guide traces. Arbitrary Python and dynamic effects limit ahead-of-time analysis; the paper supplies neither verified lowering, neural-weight composition algebra nor synthesis procedure.
interpreter_or_runtime: Python executes user control flow, PyTorch evaluates tensors/autodiff, and Pyro primitives send messages through the Poutine handler stack. Trace captures executions, replay substitutes prior site values, condition/do/lift/block/broadcast transform behavior, and inference drivers such as SVI, HMC and NUTS repeatedly interpret model/guide programs. Tag 0.3.1 code pops handlers on exceptions and checks important model-guide invariants, but user code, global parameter state and declared plate independence remain trust boundaries.
composition_rule: Ordinary Python calls/modules compose deterministic and stochastic functions; names align model and guide sites; PyTorch modules compose neural layers; Poutine messengers nest around execution and apply per-message process/postprocess transformations; trace plus replay composes posterior proposals with models; plate composes independent replicated factors and rescales subsamples. Handler order, name collisions, mutable globals, dynamic control flow and false independence declarations can change meaning, and the paper gives no formal algebra or commutation/soundness theorem for arbitrary compositions.
state_or_effect_model: Sampling, observation, learnable parameters, module registration, subsampling and inference metadata are explicit Pyro effects encoded as messages. Poutine handlers intercept them on a process-global stack; traces preserve site-level execution; the parameter store and optimizer mutate tensors; RNG state drives samples. Arbitrary Python also permits untracked I/O, mutation, exceptions and nondeterminism, so Poutine is not a general effect system for all host-language effects. Tag 0.3.1 plate documentation explicitly places conditional-independence correctness on the user.
uncertainty_model: A model denotes an execution-defined joint distribution over named latent and observed sites; a guide denotes an approximate posterior used by SVI, while HMC/NUTS target posterior sampling. Monte Carlo samples estimate ELBO terms, enumeration handles selected discrete sites and minibatch scaling estimates full-data objectives. The paper gives no denotational semantics, normalization or convergence theorem, posterior-error bound, calibration analysis, ESS/R-hat diagnostics, repeated-seed uncertainty for DMM, or uncertainty interval for reported ELBOs.

equivalence_notions.boundary: These dynamic structural checks do not prove support equality, finite variance, posterior accuracy or semantic equivalence.
Dynamic branching, site-name discipline and user code can invalidate intended alignment; no general equivalence decision procedure is supplied.
Estimator bias/variance depends on choices and the paper does not prove convergence or compare estimates with exact targets.
Exact ELBO values, seeds, traces, logs and equivalence tests are not published in the paper.
The Pyro implementation uses Monte Carlo rather than analytic KL, and one result per configuration without uncertainty does not establish reproducible equality or superiority.

lifecycle_and_provenance: The exact six-page JMLR PDF matches the resolver hash and carries CC BY 4.0. The associated MIT repository moved from uber/pyro to pyro-ppl/pyro while retaining history; release 0.3.1 at commit 92af2196 is six days after the paper's last prepublication code commit and asserts its version in VAE/DMM examples. CI covered Python 2.7/3.6 with PyTorch 1.0.1.post2 and multiple lint, docs, unit, integration, notebook and example jobs, but setup requirements are not fully locked. The paper provides no immutable code commit, container, dataset hash, experiment command, hardware receipt, logs, checkpoints, security threat model, compatibility horizon, migration/rollback policy or retirement record. Current repository success cannot be projected backward as exact 2019 experiment reproducibility.
limitations_and_failure_boundaries: The paper's universal label means expressiveness through Python control flow and probabilistic primitives; it does not prove termination, normalization, decidability or tractable inference for arbitrary programs.
There is no formal semantics or handler-composition soundness proof in the six-page system paper.
Only sample and param are Pyro primitives, but arbitrary Python permits mutation, I/O, exceptions and nondeterminism outside Poutine's visibility.
The global handler stack and global parameter store create order, naming and state interactions that are not specified by a static effect system.
Model-guide site and shape checks are necessary structural checks, not proof that the guide's support covers the posterior or that ELBO gradients are reliable.
plate correctness relies on the user truthfully declaring conditional independence; subsampling then rescales factors on that assumption.
Arbitrary dynamic control flow can create changing trace structures and frustrate static analysis, JIT compilation and reliable site alignment.
Generic inference availability does not imply all algorithms apply to every model or mix/converge efficiently.
The VAE experiment uses one GPU and four architecture settings; identical test ELBO is asserted without values or uncertainty.
VAE timing excludes end-to-end training, data loading, memory use, compilation cost and hardware diversity.
The DMM table supplies no repeated seeds, error bars, convergence curves, train/validation dispersion or statistical test.
The DMM implementation changes analytic KL to Monte Carlo estimation, limiting direct equivalence to the cited baseline.
The existing-system table is explicitly simplified and author-coded; it is not a controlled benchmark or exhaustive capability audit.
Tag 0.3.1 is publication-near rather than an exact paper-pinned commit, and its environment dependencies are only partially pinned.
Code examples and tests survive, but paper result logs/checkpoints and machine-readable Figure 3-4 receipts do not.
No independent historical-environment rerun was performed here, so code audit must not be described as reproduced empirical validation.
The paper does not define an ignition FunctionSpec, neural-weight composition law, general equivalence checker, governed asset registry or ignition probability law.
what_the_paper_does_not_support: It does not prove that arbitrary Pyro programs define valid normalized distributions, terminate or admit accurate generic inference.
It does not prove Poutine handler order is semantics-preserving or track all Python side effects.
It does not establish numerical superiority, posterior calibration or exact reproducibility from the two small experiment tables.
It does not provide weight-space composition, general program equivalence, governed Function OS lifecycle closure or ignition validation.
It does not turn a model review or code audit into formal proof or empirical validation of ignition.

paper_core_claims.claim: MUSE-Autoskill treats skills as structured, long-lived assets governed by a unified creation, memory, management, evaluation and refinement lifecycle.
A SKILL.md-centered package with optional code/tests/resources, progressive catalog disclosure, sandbox execution, per-skill memory and failure-triggered repair enables reuse across tasks and agents.
A conversation DAG with two-level summarization and immutable history plus session snapshots supports long-horizon and cross-session work.
paper_core_claims.anchors: section 3.4; Figure 4; appendices D and G

paper_core_claims.claim: On the selected 75-task SkillsBench common set and 100 SkillLearnBench instances, MUSE reports the highest compared no-skill, human-skill and self-created-skill scores under a shared GPT-5.5 backend.
Skills generated from successful trajectories transfer to Hermes and can be more accurate and cheaper on their covered task subset, while incomplete generation coverage remains the main bottleneck.

function_concept_used_by_paper: A skill is an externalized agent function packaged as a directory: its natural-language SKILL.md declares name, description, triggers, principles, tools and workflow, while optional scripts implement procedures, tests check selected behavior and resources/references supply passive context. A catalog routes tasks to skills; an LLM may create or patch packages; the agent interprets the instructions and executes scripts. This is an operational capability abstraction rather than a formal mathematical function or typed software interface.
representation_or_carrier: The carrier is a kebab-case directory with YAML-frontmatter SKILL.md and optional scripts/, tests/, resources/ and references/. Per-agent experience lives in a sibling .memory.md excluded from the shipped tarball. The bank is a filesystem directory; eager name/description YAML forms the catalog. Session state includes instruction, inputs, outputs, final response, stdout, ordered events.jsonl, short memory, a serialized conversation DAG, profiling and run metadata. Execution occurs in a process/container sandbox rooted at /sandbox.
specification_language: SKILL.md provides a natural-language schema for name, description, when-to-use triggers, core invariants, recommended tools and stepwise workflow; prose says creation additionally receives purpose, inputs and expected outputs. It has no formal type system, machine-checkable pre/postconditions, effects, permissions, dependency/environment lock, resource budgets, security classification, provenance fields, semantic version, compatibility range or deprecation state. Only directory/name consistency and optional pytest behavior are concrete checks described.
compiler_or_generator: The LLM-based skill_create procedure distills a high-level intent or successful trajectory into SKILL.md and optional scripts/resources/tests, then may call update_skill after failures. This is generative synthesis, not a verified compiler: the paper gives no released prompt/code, deterministic lowering, syntax/type checker, provenance-preserving transformation or guarantee that the generated package generalizes beyond its source task.
interpreter_or_runtime: A master ReAct agent reads the catalog, loads a selected SKILL.md, optionally reads resources, invokes sandbox lifecycle tools for scripts, observes outputs and decides further actions. Unit tests block registration only when tests exist; otherwise source-trajectory, sandbox and runtime checks are used. The runtime also maintains memory, a conversation DAG, summarization and session snapshots. There is no published executable artifact with which to independently inspect or rerun these mechanisms.
composition_rule: Skills compose informally through the master agent's planning and successive invocations; overlapping packages may be merged and entire agents are proposed as future skills. Retrieval is LLM selection from eagerly injected names/descriptions, not a measured ranking algorithm. The paper does not specify input/output unification, effect compatibility, transactionality, dependency resolution, conflict/ordering semantics, merge correctness or composition tests.
state_or_effect_model: Execution produces ordered plan/action/observation events, files, tool calls, outputs, resource use and failure feedback inside a sandbox; session and skill memories append observations; update/merge/prune mutate the bank; context compression rewires the active parent chain but retains immutable history pointers. This is useful operational tracing but not a formal effect system. Process/container isolation alone does not prove that network calls or external services have no side effects, and no permission, capability, secret, concurrency or rollback policy is specified.
uncertainty_model: The agent/model is stochastic at provider-default decoding, and SkillsBench repeats each task five times. The paper reports task-level standard deviation and stability summaries but no explicit random seeds, temperature/top-p values, paired confidence intervals, hypothesis tests or multiplicity control. SkillLearnBench instances run once per headline condition. Uncertainty about generated-skill correctness is handled heuristically through tests/runtime feedback, not probabilistically calibrated confidence.

validation_regime.skillsbench: 75 tasks shared by four runtimes, five independent Docker runs per agent/task/configuration, automated final-artifact reward in [0,1], strict 375-run denominator with uncovered generated-skill tasks scored zero
validation_regime.skilllearnbench: 20 tasks and 100 verified instances, one run per headline condition; a separate two-pass memory ablation reports 100 instances per memory condition
validation_regime.headline: MUSE reports 46.95/59.67/53.42 percent without/human/self-created skills on SkillsBench and 43/72/48 percent on SkillLearnBench
validation_regime.generation: MUSE creates usable skills for 47/75 tasks; 85.24 percent covered-subset reward exceeds 81.17 percent human-skill reward on the same selected subset, while all-task self-created reward is 53.42 percent
validation_regime.transfer: Hermes with MUSE-created skills reports 82.8 percent on the MUSE-covered subset and 51.90 percent with uncovered tasks zeroed, versus 64.3 percent human-skill reward on that covered subset
validation_regime.artifact_audit: authors manually inspect 50 MUSE packages across 47 tasks; 90 percent are SKILL.md-only, eight percent contain scripts and eight percent contain tests; one reported HVAC regression falls from 80 to 20 percent
validation_regime.formal: none; tests and automated verifiers are behavioral checks, not proofs
validation_regime.reproducibility: no MUSE code, generated skill bank, prompts, per-run outputs, events.jsonl, run_meta, containers, verifier receipts, model API receipts or exact scripts are released in the paper/source archive

equivalence_notions.boundary: Natural-language compatibility does not establish equivalent execution across agents, tools, environments or dependency versions.
Only four of 50 audited MUSE packages contain tests; generated tests may share the generator's assumptions and cannot prove correctness or generalization.
Same-task selection and reruns measure reuse under task-specific conditions, not semantic equivalence to the source procedure or out-of-distribution behavior.
Only one target agent is tested; per-skill memory is deliberately excluded from transfer, and no pairwise significance or environment-compatibility proof is reported.
Recovering source events is not equivalent to preserving all decision-relevant information in model-generated summaries.

lifecycle_and_provenance: The paper defines a useful five-stage lifecycle and supplies concrete paths for skill/session artifacts, ordered event logs and append-only memories. Yet the skill schema has no version, content hash, author/source trajectory, generator/model/prompt, creation time, dependency lock, permissions, test coverage, approval, compatibility, supersession, rollback, revocation or retirement fields. Merge/prune/refinement are prose operations without released algorithms or audit receipts; versioning is described as a planned production feature, not the evaluated bank. Per-skill experience is intentionally excluded from transferred tarballs, so transferred skills are not the same experience-aware assets used locally. The exact paper/source bytes are CC BY 4.0 and hash-bound, but no system artifact or experiment archive is public; even the printed July 7 date postdates arXiv's v2 timestamp of July 3.
limitations_and_failure_boundaries: The preprint is under review and supplies no public MUSE implementation or result archive.
The five lifecycle stages are an architectural taxonomy; creation, refinement, merge, prune and lifecycle versioning are not separately ablated or formally specified.
Only 47 of 75 selected SkillsBench tasks receive a usable MUSE skill; 28 uncovered tasks are concentrated in Ops & Planning and Data Analysis.
The evaluation excludes 19 of the 94 SkillsBench tasks because all four runtimes could not run them locally; the paper says excluded environments may be harder.
Each generated skill is distilled from one successful trajectory and rerun on the same task, creating selection and within-task overfitting risks.
The 85.24 versus 81.17 percent comparison is conditional on MUSE's successfully covered subset and must not be generalized to all 75 tasks.
A reported HVAC skill regresses from 80 to 20 percent because source-run calibration assumptions fail on fresh runs.
Only one cross-agent target, Hermes, is tested; full pairwise transfer and task/environment drift remain untested.
Transferred packages exclude .memory.md, so the transfer experiment tests procedure portability rather than transfer of accumulated per-skill experience.
Of 50 MUSE packages, 90 percent contain only SKILL.md and only eight percent contain tests; unit-test-driven wording does not characterize most generated packages.
Sandbox/runtime survival is weaker than correctness and can miss silent errors, underspecified outputs, adversarial inputs and unsafe external side effects.
A process/container filesystem does not by itself prove the paper's claim that no skill execution can affect host or external state; network/API capabilities and secrets are unspecified.
The natural-language skill interface lacks typed inputs/outputs, formal effects, dependency/environment pinning and machine-checkable pre/postconditions.
Catalog cost is not flat in bank size as claimed: injecting every name/description is linear in the number and length of entries, even though it avoids eagerly loading bodies.
Long-term and skill memories grow without compression, retention, conflict resolution, quality scoring or poisoning defenses.
Append-only Markdown is claimed safe for concurrent sessions without a described lock, atomic append protocol or conflict test.
Merge, overlap detection, retrieval, pruning and forgetting criteria are described qualitatively and receive no accuracy, conflict or provenance evaluation.
All compared agents share a named GPT-5.5 deployment but use provider-default decoding, and the paper releases no API receipt, seed or exact prompt/tool configuration for independent control.
SkillsBench has five runs per task but no paired confidence intervals or hypothesis tests; task-level standard deviations mix easy/hard tasks rather than quantify treatment uncertainty.

SkillLearnBench headline cells are single-run per instance, and the separate memory ablation uses verifier feedback and sequential within-task state that should not be pooled with the headline result.
Cost accounting is incomplete and nonuniform across agents; covered-subset medians differ by agent and do not establish system-wide cost superiority.

Production adoption claims name SkillMarket, ArkClaw and SkillHub without deployment counts, reliability incidents, independent metrics or public receipts; some listed capabilities are explicitly planned.
The public FDABench row corroborates three aggregate values but is named for a ByteDance team rather than MUSE and cannot attribute performance to the skill lifecycle.
The paper's self-evolving label is not supported by a long-duration bank-evolution study across drift, adversarial updates, version rollback or retirement.
No formal equivalence, probabilistic semantics, weight-space composition or general effect calculus is provided.
what_the_paper_does_not_support: It does not establish a formally specified, versioned and provenance-complete registry of reusable functions.
It does not prove generated skills correct, safe, equivalent across agents or robust outside the task that produced their source trajectory.
It does not show that all five lifecycle stages or per-skill memory independently cause the headline gains.
It does not establish domain-general superiority, full-benchmark coverage, production reliability or reproducible cost advantage.
It does not provide weight-space composition, stochastic ignition semantics, a general effect tracker or empirical validation of ignition.

GAP-015.reason: SKILL.md gives a portable natural-language interface and workflow schema, but lacks typed, effect-aware, provenance-aware and machine-checkable contracts.

GAP-016.reason: LLM skill creation compiles trajectories/intents into packages empirically, without verified lowering or neural-weight composition.

GAP-017.reason: Tests, same-task reruns and one cross-agent transfer provide behavioral comparisons, not semantic or general equivalence.

GAP-018.reason: Events, sandbox observations and failure feedback expose operational effects, while host/external effects, permissions, transactions and composition remain unmodeled.

GAP-019.reason: The filesystem bank, catalog, metadata, memory and maintenance operations are strong registry design evidence, but evaluated skills have no versions/hashes/provenance and versioning is planned rather than demonstrated.

GAP-020.reason: Run-to-run stochasticity is measured descriptively; no probabilistic or stochastic semantics for skills or ignition is defined.

N1_FunctionSpec.reason: SKILL.md specifies names, descriptions, triggers, principles and workflows in natural language without formal contracts.

N2_Representation.reason: Skill directories, optional code/tests/resources, memories, catalog entries, events and session DAG snapshots are concrete carriers.

N3_Compiler.reason: skill_create distills intent/trajectories into packages, but no released or verified compiler exists.

N4_Artifact.reason: The paper defines inspectable package and session schemas, but releases neither MUSE nor the evaluated packages/traces.

N8_ComposerRouter.reason: Progressive catalog disclosure and LLM routing enable reuse, while retrieval/merge/composition semantics and scalability are not evaluated.

paper_core_claims.claim: For finite-state, deterministic procedural environments, reusable skills can be conceptualized as parameterized control-flow subgraphs shared by multiple successful traces.
SKILL-DISCO approximates latent PFSM discovery through LLM trace normalization, subgoal extraction and semantic clustering, then compiles clusters into explicit contracts and Python functions.
Execution-grounded checks discard or regenerate functions that fail runtime, postcondition or action-saving requirements on a held-out set.
Author-reported ALFWorld and WebArena evaluations show higher success and fewer agent turns than matching ReAct/CodeAct agents and prior offline workflow/skill baselines.

A GPT-4o-induced library transfers without modification to five additional model configurations, and compact compiled libraries show fewer execution errors and shorter invoked procedures than ASIoffline.

function_concept_used_by_paper: A primitive function/operator has input/output spaces plus pre/post predicates and is assumed deterministic. A procedural skill is first idealized as a parameterized PFSM control-flow subgraph supported by multiple successful traces, then realized operationally as a Python function over typed domain parameters and a global environment. It invokes primitive env.step actions, branches on observations and returns success, the latest observation/available actions and a process trace.
representation_or_carrier: The theoretical carrier is a finite deterministic FSM, its latent PFSM, parameter assignments and trace subgraphs. The implemented intermediate representation is LLM-emitted Python-like control flow with symbolic variables, observations and primitive calls. Extracted operations contain a name, summary, primitive sequence and code. Clusters become JSON contracts containing signatures, descriptions, typed/default parameters, return type, pre/postconditions, declared side effects, canonical actions, abstraction level, estimated action savings and a confidence score; emitted Python and a prompt-visible library are the deployed carriers.
specification_language: Stage 4 defines a concrete JSON contract schema with callable name, typed parameters/defaults, Dict return, natural-language description/docstring, preconditions, postconditions, declared side effects, canonical action templates, abstraction level, action-savings estimate and confidence. This is stronger than a free-form skill document, but its types/predicates/effects are strings for LLM guidance rather than statically checked assertions; the code examples do not embed contract monitors, permissions, dependencies, resource bounds, provenance, versions or compatibility metadata.
compiler_or_generator: Five LLM-driven transformations normalize raw traces, extract operations, group then consolidate semantic clusters, create contracts and synthesize Python. This is a corpus-level generative compiler only by analogy: neither the latent PFSM nor lifting/matching function is computed exactly, Stage 3 uses semantic prompts including a when-in-doubt merge bias, and no preservation/soundness theorem connects traces, inferred structure, contract and code. Failed functions are reportedly regenerated up to R times, but R and the validation-set construction are not reported.
interpreter_or_runtime: At inference, every skill signature/description is appended to the agent prompt; the LLM chooses either a skill or primitive action. A selected Python function calls a global env.step, branches on observations/admissible actions and returns structured state. This can collapse multiple primitive steps into one agent turn. The WebArena example depends on an undefined find_bid helper despite the synthesis prompt saying only env.step and the Python standard library may be used, so the published listing is not self-contained under its stated contract.
composition_rule: Primitive actions compose as Python sequences, loops and branches; parameter binding abstracts objects/locations; clusters merge operations judged semantically similar; skills expose callable signatures and can be chosen by ReAct/CodeAct agents. No skill-to-skill dependency graph, type/effect unification, conflict rule, transaction, rollback, concurrency model or proof of safe composition is supplied; all signatures/descriptions are eagerly added to the prompt, so selection degrades as libraries grow and the no-distill ablation illustrates wrong-variant routing.
state_or_effect_model: FSM transitions and observations are the theoretical state/effect carrier. Contracts declare side effects in natural language, emitted code mutates the environment through env.step and process_trace records action/observation pairs. The system does not enforce declared effects, distinguish reversible from irreversible actions, model partial observability or external I/O, control permissions/secrets, or provide rollback. Real WebArena state may include dynamic/asynchronous behavior beyond the paper's deterministic finite-state idealization.
uncertainty_model: No probabilistic semantics is defined. LLM transformation and action selection are stochastic, yet the paper reports one aggregate outcome per task/model setting without seeds, repeated trials, confidence intervals or significance tests. Confidence_score is inherited from empirical cluster coverage rather than calibrated predictive uncertainty. The deterministic-operator definition excludes stochastic/nondeterministic effects rather than modeling them.

validation_regime.formal: four definitions, one problem statement and an approximate coverage score; no theorem proves PFSM recovery, clustering correctness, contract satisfaction, compiler preservation or safe composition
validation_regime.induction_evaluation_split: ALFWorld uses 200 sampled official-train tasks for induction and 134 official unseen tasks for evaluation; WebArena uses the first 406 tasks for induction and remaining 406 for evaluation
validation_regime.verification: paper says synthesized functions are checked on a held-out set for runtime correctness, postconditions and action savings, with up to R retries, but gives neither the held-out set identity/size nor R, per-skill outcomes or separation from final evaluation
validation_regime.end_to_end: with GPT-4o, ALFWorld CodeAct rises from 96.27 to 99.25 percent and ReAct from 82.00 to 92.40; WebArena ReAct rises from 23.89 to 29.06 and CodeAct from 19.95 to 22.91, while average turns fall
validation_regime.scale_boundary: on 134 ALFWorld evaluation episodes, 96.27 to 99.25 percent corresponds to approximately four additional successes; no repeated-run uncertainty is reported
validation_regime.transfer: one GPT-4o-induced library is deployed on Qwen3.5-4B/9B, GPT-4o/mini and GPT-5-chat/mini; all table cells have nondecreasing success and fewer average turns
validation_regime.usage: author-reported execution error falls from 75.3 to 0 percent versus ASIoffline on ALFWorld and from 33.9 to 21.5 on WebArena, but error definition, call denominators and intervals are absent
validation_regime.ablation: no-distill produces 43 skills and 52.99 percent ALFWorld success; no-compile keeps natural-language procedures and reaches 97.01 percent; full five-skill library reaches 99.25 percent
validation_regime.cost: execution-only tables show some reductions but WebArena skill variants cost 5.5 and 11.9 percent more than base agents; offline induction, clustering, synthesis and verification cost is omitted
validation_regime.reproducibility: no implementation, prompts in full, traces, generated libraries, environment/container revisions, seeds, decoding settings, result logs or verification receipts are released

equivalence_notions.boundary: The PFSM and lifting function are unavailable; no exact matcher, equivalence relation or closed-form criterion is implemented.
Grouping is judgment-based, prompt-biased toward merging and has no labeled clustering evaluation, stability test or false-merge rate.
Predicates and effects are not executable contract checks, validation details are missing and published code includes an undeclared helper dependency.
This is behavioral transfer on two environments, not semantic equivalence across model prompts, tool interfaces or future environment versions.
A single benchmark/backbone comparison with no repeated trials cannot isolate general compiler correctness or reliability.

lifecycle_and_provenance: The paper describes a final callable library but supplies no skill identifier/version schema, content hash, source-trace IDs, generator prompt/model revision, validation receipt, creation time, dependency/environment lock, authorship, approval, compatibility, supersession, rollback, revocation or retirement policy. Confidence and action-savings metadata are mentioned but not shown in published library records. Only successful traces enter induction, failed candidate skills may be discarded without a ledger, and libraries are not studied under updates or environment drift. The exact paper/source archive is CC BY 4.0 and hash-bound here, but the implementation and evaluated artifacts are unavailable.
limitations_and_failure_boundaries: The formal scope is finite state/action spaces with deterministic transitions; open-ended generation, reading comprehension and nonprocedural tasks are explicitly excluded.
Observed agent traces need not reveal the underlying Markov state, and WebArena can include partial, dynamic or asynchronous state not captured by the deterministic FSM idealization.
Primitive operators are assumed to return a unique output satisfying a postcondition; stochastic, flaky, nondeterministic or externally changing tools violate this premise.
The PFSM, parameterized trace graphs and subgraph matching are conceptual targets; the actual system uses LLM-generated code and semantic grouping rather than recovering those formal objects.
The reusability score is an approximation from cluster/trace statistics, with no reported threshold, calibration or comparison to ground-truth reusable subgraphs.
Stage 3 instructs the LLM to prefer fewer/larger groups and merge when in doubt, which can collapse behaviorally distinct operations.
Only successful traces supply induction signal, so rare-success domains may lack coverage and failure-recovery skills are systematically underrepresented.
Compiler quality depends on the LLM and may yield incorrect or overly specific skills; the paper explicitly acknowledges degradation with weaker models.
Typed parameters, preconditions, postconditions and side effects are natural-language JSON fields, not enforced static or runtime contracts.
The paper does not identify the held-out verification set, retry budget R, per-skill test cases, rejection counts or whether verification data are disjoint from final evaluation.
The published WebArena skill calls find_bid without defining/importing it, conflicting with the stated self-contained/stdlib-only synthesis rule unless an undocumented runtime helper exists.
Published success checks are observation-string heuristics and can differ from authoritative environment goal predicates.
Eagerly appending every skill signature/description makes routing prompt size grow with the library; the 43-skill no-distill ablation shows substantial selection interference.
ALFWorld's strongest CodeAct gain is about four additional successes among 134 episodes; no repeats, confidence interval or paired significance is reported.
WebArena is split by first versus remaining task order with no randomization/stratification analysis, so induction/evaluation distribution balance is unknown.
Baseline implementation details, model endpoints/versions, prompts, seeds, temperature, hardware and environment revisions are not fully specified.
Execution-error percentages lack a definition, number of calls and uncertainty; they cannot be treated as verified reliability rates.
Fewer agent turns do not always mean lower input tokens or cost: both WebArena skill configurations cost more than their base agents in Appendix Table 5.
Reported cost excludes one-time trace normalization, operation extraction, two-pass clustering, contract synthesis, code generation and repeated verification.
No public code, trace corpus, generated five/20-skill libraries, validation cases or result logs permit independent reproduction.
No lifecycle versioning, provenance chain, security policy, permission/effect enforcement or rollback is demonstrated.
The paper does not address neural-weight functions, general Function OS representation interoperability or probabilistic ignition semantics.
what_the_paper_does_not_support: It does not provide an exact PFSM discovery algorithm, formal compiler-soundness result or machine-checked contract system.
It does not show correctness for stochastic, open-ended, partially observable or continuously changing tasks.
It does not establish semantic equivalence between traces, clusters, contracts and emitted skills or between executions on different models.
It does not provide a reproducible, versioned and provenance-complete skill registry.
It does not empirically validate ignition, weight-space composition or stochastic ignition semantics.

GAP-016.reason: A five-stage trace-to-program-to-cluster-to-contract-to-code generator is specified and evaluated for narrow procedural environments, without formal preservation or weight composition.

GAP-017.reason: Parameter binding, semantic clustering, runtime verification and cross-model transfer provide bounded behavioral relations, not an executable semantic equivalence checker.

GAP-018.reason: Contracts declare side effects and process traces record env.step actions, while effect declarations, permissions, external effects and composition are unenforced.

GAP-019.reason: Compact callable libraries and metadata are concrete, but there is no version/provenance/lifecycle schema or public registry artifact.

GAP-020.reason: The framework assumes deterministic transitions and reports no probabilistic semantics for skills or ignition.

N1_FunctionSpec.reason: Stage 4 defines a rich explicit skill contract, though fields are LLM-facing rather than formally enforced.

N2_Representation.reason: FSM/PFSM targets, executable program IR, operations, clusters, JSON contracts, Python functions and traces are explicit carriers.

paper_core_claims.claim: An agent's mutable external capability state can be modeled as versionable skills, executable typed tools and structured anti-pattern memory, then evolved through validated atomic bundles.
Five constrained tool lifecycle operations and cascading skill updates allow tool-level defects to be repaired while avoiding invalid intermediate configurations.
Observational activation residuals and a Lotka-Volterra-inspired interaction update capture skill complementarity/conflict and improve retrieval, mutation, merge and retirement decisions.
Progressive unit, integration and regression checks plus anti-pattern veto reduce tool errors/regressions and sustain evolution without uncontrolled library bloat.
Author-reported evaluations across OfficeQA, SealQA, WildClawBench and Qwen3.5 scales show gains over fixed/skill-only baselines and lower total evolution cost in one setting.

function_concept_used_by_paper: A skill is a versioned task-facing strategy tuple containing metadata, workflow, resources and utility; it orchestrates multiple typed executable tools. A tool is interface description, implementation and input/output signature. Skills and tools form a dependency graph and are jointly mutated by atomic bundles; failures become reusable anti-pattern functions of signature, attribution and remedy. This is a practical external-policy function ecosystem rather than a formal denotational function model.
representation_or_carrier: The primary carrier is Sigma_t=(S_t,T_t,F_t): version-tagged skill records, typed executable tool records and embedded failure/epitaph records. Evolution adds a Pareto front of full system states with ancestry, per-instance scores, skill utilities and an observational interaction matrix. Trajectories carry actions/observations; proposal bundles carry typed skill/tool diffs; unit/integration/regression results gate state admission. The paper does not publish the concrete serialization, repository layout or any actual state snapshot.
specification_language: Skills expose name, trigger, version, workflow/resources and utility; tools expose descriptions, executable bodies and I/O signatures; failure records expose signature, causal attribution and remedy/bundle ID. WRAP, EDIT, COMPOSE, SPLIT and RETIRE provide lifecycle verbs with dependency-cascade prose. Missing are a machine-readable schema, semantic version policy, executable skill pre/postconditions, general effect/permission declarations, dependency constraints, migration compatibility, signatures/approvals, secret/network scope and rollback records.
compiler_or_generator: An LLM reflector diagnoses failures and proposes arbitrary combinations of skill edits plus Tool-Smith typed operations; implementations and unit tests are LLM-generated, then integrated and regression-checked. The five operation labels constrain intent but not the code emitted inside WRAP/EDIT/COMPOSE/SPLIT. No code-generation prompt, static checker, sandbox, proof of diff conformance, deterministic build, artifact hash or compiler-preservation result is supplied.
interpreter_or_runtime: For a task, the agent retrieves skills by semantic relevance, dynamic utility, pair interaction and estimated cost, then follows workflows and invokes tools. Full candidate states are executed on minibatches and accepted into a Pareto population only after reported checks. Case studies involve document parsing, web search, Slack/Git/file tools and multimodal processing, but appear to be benchmark/simulated operations; runtime permissions, isolation, human approval and external transaction behavior are unspecified.
composition_rule: Skills compose by co-activation and shared tools; bundle mutations update interdependent skills/tools together; COMPOSE chains/parallelizes tools; SPLIT rewrites dependents; lineage merge selects higher-utility skill versions and flags negative observed interactions. Atomicity is defined as one state transition U but no transactional implementation or rollback is shown. Observational beta values are not causal compatibility proofs, and tool composition type/effect correctness is not mechanically established.
state_or_effect_model: Tool calls produce environmental effects and trajectories; bundles mutate skills, executable tools and dependencies; retirement creates durable epitaphs; external perturbations can corrupt tools. Unit/integration/regression checks provide an operational safety layer. However, the system lacks formal effects, capability/permission boundaries, isolation, idempotence, compensation, rollback, secret handling, network policy, code signing and human approval—material omissions for self-modifying Slack, Git, web and file tools.
uncertainty_model: Skill utility and pair synergy are exponential-moving-average associations computed from nonrandom skill activation logs after subtracting a category mean. Zero is assigned when pair co-occurrence is below five; values are clipped and then used as if complementarity/conflict signals. Activation, task difficulty, model behavior and evolving policies confound these estimates, and no causal design, standard error, confidence interval, calibration or sensitivity analysis is given. SealQA uses three votes from one frozen LLM judge; other headline results lack repeated model-run uncertainty.

equivalence_notions.boundary: Atomicity is mathematical notation; no transaction manager, staged deployment, failure rollback or external-effect compensation is implemented in the paper.
Utilities are confounded observational estimates; tools and failure memory are not fully specified in Algorithm 3's merge, and behavioral equivalence is untested.
Nonrandom retrieval and evolving tasks/policies make beta associational, not a causal or semantic compatibility relation.
The released paper provides no per-version regression suite/results, and headline denominators contradict the declared held-out split.
Embedding proximity cannot decide functional equivalence; thresholds have no precision/recall or safety analysis.

lifecycle_and_provenance: SkillSmith is unusually explicit about skill versions, state lineages, bundle IDs, retirement patience, tool supersession and epitaphs, and therefore supplies strong lifecycle design evidence. It nevertheless omits concrete serialization, immutable content hashes, source author/model/prompt, timestamps, dependency/environment locks, test receipts, approvals, compatibility ranges, release channels, deployment status, rollback/restore mechanics and security review. Tool records do not include a version field in the formal tuple even though case studies call them v1/v2. The paper publishes no evolved state or registry, so claimed inspectability/transferability/version governance cannot be independently audited.
limitations_and_failure_boundaries: The exact PDF is a first-version preprint and no SkillSmith system artifact is released.
Table 1 uses all 246 OfficeQA and all 111 SealQA questions, directly contradicting the appendix claim that final results use only 205/92 held-out test questions.
Because train and validation questions are included in the headline denominator, the reported values cannot be treated as exclusively held-out generalization results.
WildClawBench evolves and reports over the same 38-task pool without a described held-out set; repeated improvement can reflect task-specific adaptation.
No headline confidence intervals, repeated seeds or significance tests support words such as significantly or monotonically beyond displayed point estimates.
Exact Qwen3.5 checkpoint identifiers, serving stack, prompts, temperature, seeds, quantization and hardware are absent.
The ecological utility difference compares nonrandom activated versus nonactivated executions and remains confounded after subtracting category means.
Pairwise beta estimates require only five co-occurrences, have no uncertainty/shrinkage beyond zeroing sparse pairs and cannot establish complementarity or conflict causally.
Positive/negative interaction estimates feed retrieval and mutation, creating feedback loops that can reinforce early noise; clipping masks rather than resolves instability.
Cold-start pair interactions are zero and the authors explicitly acknowledge sparse-cooccurrence noise.
The radar-chart factor gains are separate high-tercile correlations across mutually correlated complexity variables, not factorized causal contributions.
The instance Pareto algorithm does not show how the stated capacity k=3 is enforced, and tie-heavy per-instance winners can expand/oscillate.
LLM-generated causal attributions in anti-pattern records are not independently verified; false attribution can veto useful repairs.
Fourteen vetoes and 11 blocks do not report false-positive/false-negative rates, downstream harm or the three nonblocked outcomes.
Typed lifecycle labels constrain the operation category, not the arbitrary LLM-generated code inside tool modifications.
Progressive validation has no published unit-test generation method, coverage, adversarial tests, flaky-test policy or raw regression record.
Atomic bundle application is not shown to be transactional; external Slack/Git/web/file effects may occur before validation and require compensation/rollback.
Self-modifying executable tools create supply-chain and privilege-escalation risk, but sandboxing, permissions, secrets, signing and human approval are absent.
COMPOSE retains original tools, SPLIT rewrites all dependents and RETIRE removes tools, yet compatibility/migration failure handling is not specified.

Theorem A.1 validly observes a larger feasible set cannot have a worse optimum, but strict superiority is not proved: Assumption A.2 does not guarantee an evolved T* exists or solves hard and remaining tasks perfectly.
The proof's step from a missing capability to a uniform epsilon error lower bound is asserted rather than derived, and maxima/existence/compactness conditions are not supplied.
Theorem A.2 does not prove polynomial boundedness: Delta-S-dependent remains an unbounded LLM code/prompt mutation space, k is not proved constant and five operation names do not bound emitted code.
The constructed no-op tool corruption at iteration 60 advantages the method uniquely permitted to edit tools and does not establish resilience to natural distribution/API drift.
Regression rate and tool-error rate definitions/denominators are too compressed to independently validate the reported 2.1 and 3.2 percent values.
Cost Table 5 reports one run and fractional average call totals without uncertainty; the conditional gamma>rho proposition is algebraic, not a general cost guarantee.
No raw code, states, split manifests, trial logs, judge votes, costs or artifacts permit reproduction of the numerical or lifecycle claims.
The framework does not provide probabilistic semantics, neural-weight composition or general cross-representation equivalence.
what_the_paper_does_not_support: It does not establish clean held-out superiority on OfficeQA or SealQA because its published denominators include training and validation data.
It does not prove strict algorithmic superiority of joint evolution or polynomial search complexity.
It does not prove ecological beta values are causal skill synergy/conflict or that embedding similarity identifies functional anti-pattern equivalence.
It does not demonstrate safe transactional self-modification of real tools or a reproducible versioned registry.
It does not empirically validate ignition, weight-space composition or stochastic ignition semantics.

paper_core_claims.claim: Existing natural-language skills can be reorganized into a hierarchy whose lower layers expose reusable atomic capabilities and upper layers expose abstract task schemas.
A Relation Analyzer and Relation Builder can classify shared-part, subset, merge and abstract-parent relations, then rewrite source skills with explicit dependencies.
A two-stage Skill Creator uses abstract skills for task structure and atomic skills for executable detail, then incorporates each new skill through a local pyramid update.
Author-reported single-run results across 17,580 benchmark episodes show higher average reward and fewer interaction steps than four baselines.

Author-reported ablations and a GAIA-Lite subset suggest atomic, abstract and consolidation components contribute differently and that pyramidal organization can improve a filtered web-skill collection.

function_concept_used_by_paper: A skill is a structured natural-language program s=(name, description, content), where content supplies conditions, procedure and inputs/outputs; generated and rewritten SKILL.md bodies add purpose, triggers, expected context, workflow, verification, guardrails and output. Skills become nodes in a layered dependency graph and are interpreted as prompt-level procedures by an interactive LLM agent. This is an external procedural FunctionSpec architecture, not a formal denotational or executable type system.
representation_or_carrier: The primary carrier is P={L0,...,LK} over a collection of SKILL.md-like records. Atomic nodes sit below source skills, abstract nodes sit above them, and dependency references record name, identifier, reuse condition and provided capability. Analyzer assignments carry skill groups, relation type, evidence and guidance; creator inputs carry task, level/role, graph context and relevance; interactive trajectories carry observations, actions and final reward. No concrete graph serialization or evaluated library snapshot is released.
specification_language: The paper's final prompt schema is meaningfully richer than its three-field formal tuple: name/description plus Purpose, When to Use, Inputs/Expected Context, Workflow, Verification, Constraints/Guardrails and Output, with an exact textual reuse-reference form. Analyzer relation labels are SHARED_PART, SUBSET, MERGE and UPWARD_ABSTRACT_INDUCTION. These are natural-language contracts: input/output types, pre/postconditions, effects, permissions, failure taxonomy and dependency compatibility are not machine-enforced, and the claimed unique identifiers have no published generation or collision policy.
compiler_or_generator: Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-backed agents screen groups, decide relation assignments, extract/merge/canonicalize atomic skills, induce abstract skills, rewrite dependencies and generate task skills in framework/detail stages; Qwen3-Embedding-4B supports retrieval/grouping. Prompts constrain output shape and forbid invented resources, but no implementation, parser, static checker, schema validator, deterministic build, relation-consistency pass, generated-skill test, compilation receipt or preservation result is published.
interpreter_or_runtime: At evaluation time an LLM agent receives retrieved skill references inside ReAct-style ALFWorld, ScienceWorld or WebShop prompts and emits environment actions. Live feedback is said to override generated guidance. The paper reports simulated text-environment execution only; it does not specify skill-parser behavior, retrieval top-k/weights, context-budget truncation, concurrency, sandboxing, permissions, external transaction semantics or production deployment.
composition_rule: Downward extraction rewrites source skills to delegate a shared operation to a lower-level node; subset rewrites only the broader skill; merge creates one canonical skill; upward induction creates an abstract parent that composes children. The creator prioritizes high-level nodes for framework and low-level nodes for detail. Natural-language LLM judgment decides coverage and near-equivalence; similarity thresholds, merge-conflict resolution, graph-cycle checks, level-conflict handling and behavioral composition tests are absent.
state_or_effect_model: The formal trajectory contains task, observation/action sequence and final reward; skills describe environment actions and state checks; self-evolution mutates the library and pyramid. The paper does not define effect signatures, capabilities, secrets, network/file access, idempotence, rollback, compensation, approval or quarantine. Its ethics section recommends task-level access control and skill-level auditing for downstream systems, confirming these controls are outside the presented mechanism.
uncertainty_model: All headline cells come from one temperature-zero run. No repeated seed/run, confidence interval, standard error, significance test, paired task delta, judge calibration or API nondeterminism analysis is reported. Temperature zero does not by itself make hosted API calls or an evolving multi-agent process reproducible. Relation confidence is optional free-form similarity/evidence, not calibrated uncertainty; web-skill filtering and graph decisions have no error bars, precision/recall or sensitivity analysis.

The paper says new skills are validated before incorporation, but its self-evolution equation and prompts contain no admission test, reject/quarantine branch or validation receipt.
A Verification section inside generated prose tells a future agent how to check task progress; it is not evidence that the generated skill itself was validated before registry mutation.
Skills and relation evidence remain unconstrained natural language, so shared-part, subset, merge and abstraction decisions are not type- or behavior-checked.
No acyclicity, layer-consistency or dependency-integrity algorithm is supplied for repeated upward/downward extraction, merging and incremental insertion.
Similarity thresholds, coarse-group formation, retrieval top-k, stage weights, full-coverage predicate and canonical-merge rules are absent.
The initial skill-library construction procedure and size are not reported, even though it materially determines both flat and pyramid conditions.
Same initial library does not isolate hierarchy alone: SkillPyramid additionally extracts/induces/generated skills and evolves them, whereas ReAct+Skills remains flat and static.
The 38.0 percent reward improvement and 27.7 percent step reduction are relative to vanilla ReAct, not the stronger same-library ReAct+Skills control.

Table 1 contains several cells where SkillPyramid is not best, including DeepSeek WebShop reward/steps and Gemini ALFWorld seen reward, so consistent superiority is only aggregate/broad, not per condition.
All results use one temperature-zero run; no variance, paired uncertainty or significance supports stability or deterministic reproducibility.
Hosted API model versions/endpoints and system nondeterminism are not pinned; temperature zero alone cannot reproduce outputs.
Average interaction-step denominators, failed-episode treatment and maximum-step rules are not stated.
Figure 3 lacks task order, raw curve values, smoothing details and repeated-order bands, so claims of stability/convergence are visual and author-reported.
The atomic-heavy/abstract-heavy grouping depends on oracle trajectories and evaluation-set quartiles; task membership and computation are unreleased.
The GAIA-Lite sample, 150K candidate provenance and 2,271-skill quality filter are unspecified, allowing unmeasured sampling/selection sensitivity.
The GAIA-Lite backbone and exact-match/scoring implementation are not stated in the reported section/table.
The paper reports about 1.07B input/output tokens across construction, main and analyses but no monetary/latency budget or scaling benchmark for larger libraries.
The initial full-library analysis is acknowledged as a scalability bottleneck; only three outer/five inner round caps are given, not complexity or convergence.
Only two reuse axes are modeled; temporal and causal dependencies are explicitly left open.
Weaker construction backbones, multimodal/embodied settings and natural distribution drift are not evaluated.
Web-mined skills create content/supply-chain risks; access control and auditing are recommendations, not implemented parts of the framework.
No versioning, provenance-complete registry, deprecation, rollback or recovery semantics accompany destructive rewrite/merge operations.
The framework does not provide probabilistic semantics, neural-weight composition, formal program equivalence or general cross-representation equivalence.
what_the_paper_does_not_support: It does not establish a validated skill-admission lifecycle despite using the word validate in headline prose.
It does not establish deterministic reproducibility, statistical significance or per-condition superiority from a single temperature-zero run.
It does not establish semantic equivalence or safe behavior preservation for skill extraction, rewrite, merge or abstraction.
It does not demonstrate a production-safe, versioned, rollback-capable or permission-governed evolving registry.
It does not empirically validate ignition, weight-space composition or stochastic ignition semantics.
