paper_core_claims.claim: A domain knowledge tree can guide targeted mining of repositories, APIs, scripts, notebooks, documentation, databases and papers, while its linked resources, skills and validation states evolve with coverage.
Mined resources can be compiled into self-contained skill packages with scope, inputs/outputs, steps, dependencies, environment assumptions, provenance, examples, scripts, assets and tests.
Execution, system, synthetic-data and downstream utility testing can drive repair, acceptance, merging and pruning in a closed loop.

The author-reported writing-time snapshot contains 286 skills from 394 resources across 27 domains/254 subdomains, all retained skills pass required tests, and 71.1 percent are novel relative to SkillHub/SkillSMP.
Author-reported skill access improves five of six 88-task MoSciBench subsets and improves one spatial-transcriptomics annotation run and a three-replicate scDRS workflow.

function_concept_used_by_paper: A skill is a reusable package around a human-readable SKILL.md contract plus optional executable scripts, tests, assets and metadata. Its contract names task scope, dependencies, inputs/outputs, procedure, environment assumptions, provenance and examples. The public implementation realizes both runnable wrappers and many starter-plan artifacts; therefore the skill abstraction ranges from executable capability to procedural planning specification and cannot uniformly be read as an executed scientific function.
representation_or_carrier: The control carrier is a rooted domain tree whose nodes link resources, skills and validation state. Resource registries are JSONL records with topic paths, signals, scores, provenance and status. Skill registries link IDs/paths, domains/subdomains, resources, status and summaries; each filesystem package carries SKILL.md, metadata, scripts/assets/tests where available. Campaign state, worker workspaces, reports and generated dashboards are additional carriers, though campaign/experiment receipts are absent from the audited public head.
specification_language: SKILL.md is the primary natural-language contract: task purpose and scope, trigger/use conditions, required inputs, outputs, stepwise workflow, environment/dependency assumptions, examples, provenance and validation guidance. Registry/metadata JSON adds IDs, topic placement, sources and coarse status. These schemas do not machine-enforce types, pre/postconditions, declared effects, permissions, resource bounds, failure taxonomies, compatibility or scientific correctness; status implemented can denote a plan-producing starter rather than verified domain execution.
compiler_or_generator: The staged LLM pipeline maps tree gaps to resource_search, extracts source-grounded contracts through skill_build/design_skill, emits SKILL.md/scripts/assets/tests, evaluates with skill_test/layer1_fix/layer2_benchmark/layer2_optimize, checks novelty, and lets refresh update shared registries/tree/site. GPT-5.4 and GPT-5.4-mini roles are specified and concrete orchestration/prompt/repository code is public. However, published prompts are explicitly abbreviated, campaign receipts and the paper snapshot are absent, semantic preservation is not proved, and the public repository cannot reproduce the reported 286/394 build.
interpreter_or_runtime: Codex- or Claude-style agents discover and read SKILL.md, then follow prose and invoke bundled scripts in local, sandbox or Slurm contexts. Repository execution helpers isolate leaf workers, collect structured reports and restrict automatic merging to leaf-owned paths; refresh owns shared registries. The interpreter remains an LLM plus shell/Python runtime, so adherence to contracts, environment compatibility, external side effects, scientific interpretation and approval boundaries are not enforced by a formal runtime.
composition_rule: Taxonomy paths route resources and skills; leaf packages combine prose, scripts, assets and tests; refresh merges isolated leaf outputs into shared registries; novelty review discards duplicates, merges complementary scope or creates a new leaf. Composition is path/ownership- and prompt-governed rather than type/effect checked. The novelty code scores a small local candidate set with LLM/web-search assistance, not the paper's fully receipted binary comparison against named external libraries, and no merge-equivalence or regression invariant is published.
state_or_effect_model: Live state records tree coverage, linked resources/skills, validation status, campaign stages, workspace ownership and reports. Skills may execute filesystem, Python, network or cluster operations, but effect signatures, capabilities, secrets, irreversible actions, transaction boundaries, idempotence, compensation and rollback are not modeled. Isolated leaf workspaces reduce shared-file conflicts, while shared refresh is a governance convention rather than transactional composition.
uncertainty_model: The paper supplies point estimates only. MoSciBench contains 88 tasks with small per-dataset denominators of 13-17 and no repeated runs, paired confidence intervals or significance tests. The cell experiment is one clustered dataset with one reported run; cells are not independent replicates. scDRS has three replicates, but no intervals/test and one skill-assisted qualitative score is no better than the worst baseline. Novelty has no numerator, sampling frame, recall/precision, judge agreement or sensitivity; 71.1 percent cannot be a one-decimal rounded binary fraction of 286 or the public 267. LLM and web judgments are not calibrated uncertainty.

The no-change NURSE subset bounds the claim to five of six datasets rather than uniform improvement.
The spatial-cell metrics use one dataset/run; 228635 cells are clustered observations, not independent experimental repetitions.
The scDRS experiment has only three replicates and no interval/test; one with-skill qualitative score of three matches the worst baseline score.
Expert count, blinding procedure beyond the stated label, scoring rubric reliability and inter-rater agreement are not reported.
The appendix says full prompts/run counts/hardware are deferred, then explicitly states that its templates are abbreviated; instantiated prompts and run counts remain absent.
The fixed resource-mining search budget is unnamed and runtime excludes API-token use, so scaling/cost cannot be reproduced.
Internal execution of a wrapper or synthetic example does not establish downstream scientific validity; the authors themselves separate internal from utility evaluation.
Natural-language contracts and LLM generation do not establish type/effect safety, semantic preservation, scientific correctness or safe external composition.
Parallel leaf ownership reduces write conflicts but supplies no transaction, rollback, permission or external-effect semantics.
Self-evolving is demonstrated as architecture and update-log history, not as a released autonomous longitudinal campaign with before/after state and complete receipts.
Registry status/provenance are useful but not a versioned, immutable, rollback-capable lifecycle.
The system does not provide probabilistic program semantics, calibrated decision uncertainty, formal program equivalence or weight-space composition.

It does not support 71.1 percent as a reconciled binary novelty fraction of the stated library.
It does not support interpreting every public starter smoke test as execution of the named scientific capability.
It does not establish statistical significance, robust reproducibility or causal downstream improvement from the small single-run evaluations.
It does not establish semantic equivalence, safe merge preservation or scientifically correct generated skills.
It does not establish a production-safe, transactional, versioned or rollback-capable self-evolving registry.
It does not empirically validate ignition, stochastic ignition semantics or neural weight-space composition.

paper_core_claims.claim: An LLM curriculum can propose achievable, progressively harder Minecraft tasks from agent state and exploration history.
Successful LLM-generated JavaScript programs can be described, embedded, stored and retrieved as temporally extended reusable skills that compose through function calls.
Environment feedback, execution errors and GPT-4 self-verification can iteratively refine code and gate skill admission.
Across three author-run trials, Voyager finds about 3.3 times more unique items, travels 2.3 times farther and reaches early tech-tree levels up to 15.3 times faster than adapted baselines.
A learned library transfers to a new world and improves four unseen crafting/collection tasks, while top-five description retrieval is reported at 96.5 percent over 309 samples.

function_concept_used_by_paper: A skill is an async JavaScript function with one bot argument, a generated natural-language description and a task-conditioned success history. Its body composes Mineflayer/control primitives and older skills into a temporally extended policy. The active registry maps the function name to code/description and Chroma indexes the description. This is a concrete executable external function architecture, not a typed, formally specified or sandboxed function calculus.
representation_or_carrier: Minecraft state is rendered as inventory/equipment, nearby blocks/entities, biome/time, health/hunger, position, chests, completed/failed tasks, chat feedback and error events. Skills are JavaScript source plus description text, skills.json and a persistent Chroma vector index. Curriculum QA, progress, chest memory and timestamped event JSON form checkpoint state. Public trial libraries expose final active artifacts but not their event/conversation histories.
specification_language: The enforced callable surface is an async function whose sole parameter is bot; prompts require a meaningful generic name, inventory checks, reuse of provided functions and no loops/recursion. Description prose is at most six sentences. There are no typed inputs/outputs beyond bot, pre/postconditions, declared effects, permissions, dependencies, failure types, version constraints or resource bounds. Task success is a separate critic judgment rather than a contract embedded in the function.
compiler_or_generator: GPT-4 maps task/state/retrieved skills/feedback/errors/critique into JavaScript; Babel parses function declarations and selects the last async one as entry point; the program is executed and refined up to four rounds. GPT-3.5 generates descriptions and embeddings. This is a public execution-guided compiler loop, but it offers no semantic-preservation proof, static effect checking, test generation or guarantee that parser-valid code is safe/correct.
interpreter_or_runtime: Python agents send all active skills/control primitives plus the selected program to a Node/Mineflayer server, which executes the concatenated source through eval against a live bot. Chat/error/observation events return to the next prompt. The runtime is operationally concrete and supports long actions, yet generated code shares the full process and bot authority without sandboxing, time/resource quotas inside eval, capability separation or transaction boundaries.
composition_rule: Top-five description similarity selects prompt-visible skills; GPT-4 composes them and primitives through ordinary JavaScript calls, sequences, branches and awaits. All active programs are also loaded into the execution environment. Names are the registry identity. No type/effect compatibility, dependency graph, name-collision prevention across helpers, behavioral equivalence, regression testing or conflict resolution is defined.
state_or_effect_model: Environment observations and event streams expose mutable inventory, equipment, world blocks/entities, health, hunger, position, chests and time. Code performs mining, crafting, placing, smelting, combat, chest and movement effects. Some failed placement effects can be reversed and crafting tables/furnaces are recycled with commands, but arbitrary JavaScript/world effects have no typed effect signature, permission model, idempotence, compensation or general rollback.
uncertainty_model: Main curves and tables use three trials and report some means plus spread, but no seeds, confidence intervals, hypothesis tests or paired per-world analysis. Temperature zero does not remove hosted-model or world nondeterminism; curriculum uses 0.1 plus unseeded Python prompt-field sampling. Diamond mastery occurs in only one of three Voyager trials. The GPT-4-0613 comparison is visual and described as roughly the same without numeric equivalence criteria. Retrieval accuracy lacks labeling protocol, annotator agreement and class/prevalence details. No calibrated confidence governs curriculum, critic or admission decisions.

validation_regime.formal: algorithm pseudocode and syntax parsing only; no formal semantics, proof, static safety, compiler correctness or non-forgetting theorem
validation_regime.new_skill_admission: a program is admitted when it parses, executes without blocking error and the GPT-4 critic labels the task successful within four attempts; critic mistakes are acknowledged and no independent test/regression suite is created
validation_regime.exploration: three trials per method over up to 160 recorded prompting iterations; appendix releases final item lists but not world seeds, event streams, prompts/responses or exact plotting data
validation_regime.tech_tree: Voyager succeeds 3/3 on wood/stone/iron but only 1/3 on diamond; headline 15.3x uses 6 versus AutoGPT's 92 average wooden-tool iterations
validation_regime.unseen_tasks: Voyager succeeds 3/3 on four tasks; no-skill Voyager also succeeds 3/3 on three tasks and 2/3 on diamond pickaxe but takes more iterations; adapted base ReAct/Reflexion/AutoGPT score 0/3
validation_regime.retrieval: 309 author-labeled samples across the public paper report 80.2 percent top-one and 96.5 percent top-five accuracy, without released queries/relevance labels or annotation method
validation_regime.ablation: six component removals on exploration show large point differences, but raw values, repeated-world pairing and inferential uncertainty are not released
validation_regime.model_variation: v2 adds a GPT-4-0613 curve close to GPT-4-0314, but current public repository predates v2 and no numeric tolerance, logs or exact model-run artifacts are supplied

equivalence_notions.boundary: Vector similarity is a routing heuristic, not functional equivalence or substitutability.
The same model family supplies an uncalibrated judgment and acknowledged false positives/negatives; no general executable postcondition exists.
Twelve trials over four Minecraft tasks do not establish semantic preservation across arbitrary worlds, agents or domains.
Name identity does not prove behavioral equivalence; historical V2 files are retained without active lineage, comparison or rollback.

lifecycle_and_provenance: Voyager persists completed/failed tasks, QA cache, chest memory, event files, skills.json, descriptions, code and vector databases, enabling resume and cross-world library loading. Function-name collisions write a V2-style historical file while overwriting the active dictionary/vector entry; public libraries therefore have more code files than active skills. It lacks per-skill source task/trace, model/prompt/version, creation timestamp, immutable hash, dependencies, validation receipt, usage/success metrics, semantic version, approval, deprecation, tombstone, migration and active rollback pointer. Git versions the released repository, but the three libraries are final snapshots rather than complete evolution histories.
limitations_and_failure_boundaries: The exact source is arXiv v2 under the non-exclusive distribution license; the MIT code head predates v2 and has no immutable paper tag.
Generated JavaScript and the full library execute via Node eval with the bot process's authority; parser checks are not a sandbox or capability boundary.
GPT-4 self-verification is an admission heuristic, not proof of task completion, code correctness or safety; the paper documents verifier failures.
Successful admission creates no regression test, so future composition and environmental changes can silently break a skill.
An existing program name overwrites the active skill/vector record; ever-growing describes accumulated artifacts/capability intent, not a strictly append-only active registry.
Historical V2 code files lack explicit parent links, validation deltas or a restore mechanism.
All active skill code is loaded into the runtime, allowing helper-name collisions and untracked dependencies even though only top-five skills are shown to the generator.
No type/effect system governs inventory/world mutation, external authority, concurrency, idempotence or irreversible actions.
Some environment commands recycle items/blocks and optional failed placements, so measured behavior is a custom instrumented Minecraft setting rather than unrestricted survival play.
README startup requires interactive world selection/open-to-LAN and recommends monitoring; no-human-intervention is bounded to the launched learning loop, not end-to-end operation.
Main evidence uses three trials; no world/random seeds, paired analysis, confidence intervals or significance tests are supplied.
Diamond-tool success is only 1/3, so the only-method-to-unlock claim does not mean reliable mastery.
The 15.3x headline is an early wooden-tool ratio against AutoGPT, not a uniform speedup over all milestones/baselines.
ReAct, Reflexion and AutoGPT are author adaptations to MineDojo/Mineflayer rather than original out-of-box embodied systems; conclusions are conditional on those implementations.
The system uses high-level symbolic state and Mineflayer APIs, not pixels or low-level sensorimotor control, which the authors explicitly exclude.
Final item/terrain lists and libraries are public, but full baseline/Voyager event streams, model conversations, task sequences and plotting inputs are not.
Retrieval relevance labels, annotators and per-query results for 309 samples are absent.
Temperature zero and one later model curve do not establish robustness to API/model/environment variation.
Cost is substantial and endpoint-dependent; the paper gives only a 15x GPT-4/GPT-3.5 ratio, while the repository FAQ gives a historical approximate 50 USD per 160 iterations.
The repository has no automated test suite and broadly unpinned legacy dependencies; static Python compilation is not live reproduction.
Minecraft hallucinations, unachievable curriculum tasks, invalid APIs/fuels, stuck behavior and absent visual perception are acknowledged.
The evidence is Minecraft-specific and does not establish safe robotics deployment, general lifelong learning or immunity to catastrophic forgetting.
The method does not define probabilistic function semantics, calibrated uncertainty, formal equivalence or neural weight composition.
what_the_paper_does_not_support: It does not prove skill correctness, safe execution, semantic composition or non-forgetting.
It does not establish reliable diamond mastery from one success in three trials.
It does not establish deterministic reproduction, statistical significance or broad model/world robustness.
It does not establish an append-only, versioned, provenance-complete or rollback-capable registry.
It does not establish end-to-end autonomous operation without initial human/game setup.
It does not empirically validate ignition, stochastic ignition semantics or weight-space composition.

paper_core_claims.claim: NLI learns a sequence-valued discrete, symbolic-like latent language and a recurrent differentiable neural interpreter from input-output examples.
Differentiability permits test-time gradient search over latent programs, initialized by the inductor and scaled with restarts and gradient steps.
On the custom author-generated splits, gradient search reports mean OOD accuracies 0.99, 1.00 and 0.91 for Shift-L, Shift-P and Comp-I, while listed neural baselines remain much lower.
A 512-token latent vocabulary reuses token IDs as learned shift primitives, and ablations associate discrete recurrent execution with custom-benchmark OOD performance.
On five author-regenerated DeepCoder compositional splits, NLI and LPN variants are compared with supervised neuro-symbolic baselines, with complementary strengths rather than uniform dominance.

function_concept_used_by_paper: The unknown target program is treated extensionally as a mapping inferred from a finite set of input-output pairs. NLI represents a candidate as a fixed-capacity sequence of distributions over 512 opaque learned tokens, with skip tokens giving variable effective length. A recurrent neural interpreter applies one latent operation per step. This is a learned neural function representation, not source code, a human-readable DSL program, a typed callable contract or a formally defined symbolic semantics.
representation_or_carrier: Specifications are finite sets of input-output pairs. The inductor mean-pools per-example transformer embeddings into T categorical token distributions; Gumbel-Softmax approximates discrete samples. The interpreter carries a recurrent hidden execution state and token-conditioned neural layer choices. During test-time search, Gaussian-initialized continuous embeddings are optimized and the final prediction uses their soft distributions, so the operational artifact need not be a hard token sequence even when training visualizations show discrete IDs.
specification_language: The only general specification language is extensional examples S={(x_i,y_i)} plus a new input. Custom tasks operate on fixed-length sequences, and DeepCoder supplies integer/list input-output examples from a known experimental DSL. No user-facing names, type declarations, signatures, pre/postconditions, effects, permissions, resources, failure modes, dependencies or lifecycle constraints are compiled. DeepCoder ground-truth program text is used only by explicitly supervised comparison variants, whose program encoder is discarded at test time.
compiler_or_generator: The program inductor maps a finite specification to token-distribution sequences; test-time gradient descent refines latent embeddings through the differentiable interpreter using 100 steps and up to 8192 parallel initializations in the custom Comp-I setting. This is a concrete neural synthesis/search pipeline. It does not emit executable code, prove semantic preservation, guarantee a discrete result, check types/effects, generate tests or certify the inferred behavior beyond finite examples.
interpreter_or_runtime: A recurrent neural executor consumes one program token distribution at a time, updates a hidden state and predicts the output distribution. Skip is a learned no-op and makes effective program length variable. The runtime is an internal differentiable neural computation, not a released engine for executing named external functions; it has no branches, loops, parameterized instructions, observable call stack, effect isolation, sandbox or resource policy.
composition_rule: Composition is ordered concatenation/repetition of latent token positions, interpreted recurrently. The shift example reuses IDs 231 and 476, and gradient search can construct longer sequences. Token identities are opaque and empirical; there is no typed compatibility relation, algebraic law, branch/control composition, named dependency graph, equivalence checker or proof that a token denotes the same operation across seeds, domains or retraining.
state_or_effect_model: The recurrent hidden execution state mediates sequential transformations of value representations. Benchmarks are pure input-output sequence/list tasks, so external effects, mutation permissions, exceptions, concurrency, transactions, compensation, idempotence, rollback and environment state are outside the model. The hidden state is not exposed as an execution trace or governed effect record.
uncertainty_model: Training and interpretation use categorical distributions, Gumbel noise and probabilistic output likelihoods, while test-time search uses multiple Gaussian starts. These are optimization/representation mechanisms, not calibrated semantic uncertainty over synthesized functions. Custom headline values are means over three seeds but Table 1 gives no variance, confidence intervals, per-seed results or statistical tests. Figure-only DeepCoder values lack a numerical table and uncertainty. The source provides no seeds, checkpoints, logs or calibration analysis, and the 11.6-million DeepCoder training count in the main text/Table 3 conflicts with 2 million in appendix prose.

validation_regime.formal: the paper supplies objectives, algorithms and a differentiable regularizer derivation, but no theorem, formal semantics, mechanized proof, compiler-correctness result or equivalence guarantee
validation_regime.custom_benchmark: three author-generated synthetic splits, all models trained for 100k batches of 512 and reported as three-seed means; NLI Gradient Search reports 0.99/1.00/0.91 OOD, but no variances, per-seed outputs, significance tests or released data/code are supplied
validation_regime.custom_ablation: component removals are plotted as average OOD accuracy and temperature schedules are reported for Shift-L ID; exact per-split/per-seed values and raw receipts are absent, and the temperature table validates ID rather than OOD compositional generalization

equivalence_notions.boundary: Agreement on finitely many examples does not establish extensional equality on the input domain, semantic equivalence or correctness.
This is an empirical interpretation from one trained setting, not a stable named operator contract across seeds or domains.
The final operational representation is not guaranteed to correspond to a concrete discrete program or readable symbolic expression.
High accuracy on three synthetic split families is not a general semantic-preservation or program-equivalence result.

lifecycle_and_provenance: NLI defines training, inference and search phases, but it does not maintain a registry of synthesized functions. Latent tokens have numeric IDs only; there is no immutable artifact hash, human-readable meaning, source specification record, model/checkpoint lineage, dependency list, validation receipt, semantic version, approval, usage history, deprecation, tombstone, migration or rollback. Retraining can change token meaning, and test-time optimized soft representations are per-task ephemeral states. The paper/source version is traceable, but the trained languages and synthesized programs are not released.
limitations_and_failure_boundaries: The method infers behavior from finite examples; it does not establish full-domain correctness or equivalence.
Final gradient-search inference uses soft latent representations, so symbolic-like and discrete training language must not be restated as guaranteed concrete symbolic programs.
Latent token IDs are opaque learned operations without human-readable definitions, types or stable cross-run identity.
The interpreter supports strictly sequential programs and omits branches, loops and parameterized primitives such as add(k), as the authors acknowledge.
Skip changes effective length within a fixed maximum T; arbitrary length remains bounded by configured representation/search capacity and training details.
Test-time search can require 1024 or 8192 initializations and 100 gradient steps; scaling results do not include normalized runtime, memory or energy comparisons.
The custom benchmark uses synthetic fixed-length sequence tasks and over 20 simple primitives; near-perfect OOD results do not establish general software synthesis.
Custom Table 1 reports only three-seed means and no uncertainty; no raw per-seed values or significance tests are released.
Ablation plots aggregate datasets and omit exact numerical/per-seed tables; association does not isolate a universal causal mechanism.
The Gumbel-temperature table reports Shift-L ID accuracy, not OOD compositional accuracy.
DeepCoder data are regenerated because the original compositional training data are unavailable, so comparisons are conditional on a new unreleased corpus.
DeepCoder training size is internally inconsistent: 11.6 million in main text/Table 3 versus 2 million in appendix prose.
DeepCoder results appear only as a plot without numerical values, variability or statistical tests.
Program-supervised NLI/LPN variants and neuro-symbolic baselines have materially different supervision, limiting headline comparisons.
Competitive with ExeDec is split-dependent; the figure does not support uniform parity or superiority.
No code, generated data, checkpoints, seeds, run logs, search trajectories or plotting inputs are linked or included.
No external side-effect model, safety policy, sandbox, lifecycle registry or provenance for synthesized programs is defined.
Categorical/Gumbel distributions do not provide calibrated uncertainty or probabilistic function semantics.
The model review checks the released record but is not a reproduction of the reported experiments.
what_the_paper_does_not_support: It does not prove correctness, semantic equivalence, completeness or safety of synthesized programs.
It does not establish that the final searched representation is a discrete, readable or executable symbolic program.
It does not establish general-purpose program synthesis beyond the reported synthetic and DeepCoder domains.
It does not establish calibrated uncertainty, probabilistic function semantics or statistically significant superiority.
It does not provide a versioned/provenance-complete function registry or lifecycle protocol.
It does not empirically validate ignition, external Function OS deployment or weight-space composition.

paper_core_claims.claim: A subset of Forth can be represented as a differentiable dual-stack abstract machine whose program sketches mix fixed words with trainable transition slots.
The trainable slot language exposes static/observe/linear/sigmoid/tanh encoders and choose/manipulate/permute decoders, optimized from only initial and target machine states.
Symbolic execution and interpolation of branch-free branches reduce recurrent execution work, while loops/function calls can still require full unrolling.
Strong procedural sketches can learn sorting and addition from small synthetic sets and generalize to longer test sequences when the intended discrete behavior is learned.
A BiLSTM plus differentiable Forth sketch reaches 96 percent on the 200-item Common Core test set, one point above the cited same-data Seq2Seq result and below a 98.5-percent data-augmented baseline.

function_concept_used_by_paper: A function is a Forth word or subroutine interpreted as a machine-state transition w:S→S. A program is a sequence/composition of such transitions, and a sketch replaces selected transitions with trainable neural slots. This is a concrete hybrid symbolic-neural function architecture, but the learned behavior is identified by finite input-output loss rather than a proof of semantic equivalence.
representation_or_carrier: The symbolic carrier is low-level Forth code plus stack comments and sketch slots. The differentiable carrier is S=(D,R,H,c): matrix-valued data and return stacks with soft pointers, a heap and an attention-valued program counter. Slot encoders observe named state elements; decoders emit weighted Forth-word choices or direct linear/softmax state transformations. Training artifacts are neural parameters, but no serialized checkpoint or code package is released.
specification_language: The external specification combines an ordinary Forth subset with slots written `{ encoder -> decoder }`. Encoders are static, observe and repeated linear/sigmoid/tanh transformations; decoders are choose, manipulate and permute over named words/state elements. Stack-effect comments and fixed control structure express intended interfaces. The language has no static types beyond shapes/addresses, no declared pre/postconditions, effects, permissions, failure modes, uncertainty, version constraints or resource bounds.
compiler_or_generator: A Forth sketch is lowered to low-level code with branches, jumps and labeled subroutine blocks; each slot is replaced by a parameterized neural transition. Symbolic execution collapses branch-free known-word sequences and certain if-branches are interpolated in parallel. Gradient descent then fits slot parameters from start/end states. This is a concrete described hybrid compiler/trainer, but the implementation is not released and no lowering or semantic-preservation proof is supplied.
interpreter_or_runtime: The ∂4 execution RNN repeatedly applies every low-level transition to the current continuous state and weights next states by the soft program counter. Data/return-stack pointers, heap addressing, calls, loops and branches are differentiable approximations of the Forth machine. At test time transduction memory is discretized. The runtime is described through equations, listings and traces, but no executable public runtime was audited, and external non-differentiable effects are explicitly future work.
composition_rule: Forth concatenation, subroutine calls, recursion, loops and branches compose known transitions; sketches splice trainable slots into this control skeleton. Symbolic execution composes branch-free sequences into one transition, while branch interpolation weights two branch outputs. Composition is structural and operational, not governed by type/effect compatibility, learned-module contracts, equivalence checking, regression tests or capability boundaries.
state_or_effect_model: The state model explicitly contains two mutable stacks, a random-access heap and a program counter, with differentiable read/write, push/pop, arithmetic, comparisons, jumps and subroutine control. These are internal machine effects inside a fixed tensor runtime. No model is provided for filesystem/network/robot/environment authority, irreversible actions, transactions, idempotence, compensation, rollback or concurrent interference; real-environment non-differentiable transitions are deferred to future work.
uncertainty_model: The learned program counter and word selections may be distributed during training and are discretized for some tests, but these soft weights are optimization representations rather than calibrated epistemic or aleatoric uncertainty. The paper reports point accuracies and a relative-runtime plot from ten repeats, yet gives no model-run seed count, variance/confidence intervals, significance tests, calibration, failed-run denominator or raw run data. Randomly generated datasets and random hyperparameter search are described without seeds. Consequently the exact stability and reproducibility of the neural results are unresolved.

limitations_and_failure_boundaries: The exact registered PMLR PDF and supplement are source-complete, but no paper-authored executable runtime, checkpoint, dataset package or experiment ledger was identified.
The implementation covers only a subset of Forth; Turing completeness of the language does not imply complete Forth compatibility or practical scalability of ∂4.
Continuous stacks, heap addressing and program counters approximate symbolic machine state and can accumulate numerical ambiguity.
The correspondence between one-hot recurrent execution and symbolic execution is stated rather than formally proved or exhaustively tested.
Finite input-output supervision underdetermines slot semantics and cannot establish behavioral equivalence on all states.
Sorting generalization is conditional: both sketches score 100 percent after length-2/3 training but fail badly when trained on length 4.
The paper attributes length-4 failure to long unrolled execution and training instability; BubbleSort at input length 4 uses 120 machine states.
The Permute sketch does not always converge to an output of the correct length, and both sketches are described as nontrivial to train.
The stronger Compare and Choose results depend on substantial human-supplied algorithmic scaffolding, so learned capability should not be attributed to unconstrained program induction.
Test-time discretization is part of the displayed transduction results and changes the continuous training regime.
The claimed perfect length-24-to-128 addition experiment is not accompanied by a table, per-run data or artifact receipt.
Common Core has only 200 test items; the 96-percent result is one point above the cited same-data Seq2Seq result and below the 98.5-percent extra-data GeNeRe result.
The WAP system predicts final answers directly and does not produce the explicit formula representation used by template-mapping systems, limiting interpretability claims.
No model seed count, error bars, confidence intervals, significance tests or failed-run accounting is reported for accuracy results.
The runtime plot uses ten repeats but omits absolute time, hardware, raw measurements and executable benchmarking code.
Hyperparameter search uses development data but has no released search space, selected-trial ledger or seed.
The machine effect model is internal tensor memory only; non-differentiable transitions in real environments are explicitly future work.
No type/effect/capability system, sandbox, transaction, compensation or rollback boundary is defined.
No versioned registry, provenance-complete learned-slot package, admission receipt or lifecycle governance is present.
This review checks documentary evidence and source integrity; it does not reproduce the experiments or independently validate their measurements.

It does not prove compiler/lowering correctness, numerical fidelity or safe execution.
It does not establish reliable optimization for longer unrolls; its length-4 sorting results show the opposite boundary.
It does not establish a released, reproducible, production-ready differentiable Forth system.
It does not provide external effect contracts, permissions, transactions, rollback or a versioned artifact registry.
It does not define calibrated stochastic function semantics or uncertainty-aware admission.
It does not empirically validate ignition, Function OS deployment or neural-weight composition.
The model review is not proof or independent empirical validation of the authors' experiments.

paper_core_claims.claim: A compiler for a substantial pure Scheme subset can compile its own evaluator into a differentiable PyTorch computation graph with closures, recursion, pairs/lists and runtime-supplied programs.

paper_core_claims.claim: Within terminating trace-constant regions, the compiled interpreter preserves source values and reverse-mode gradients almost everywhere, and this property is preserved under composition.
Released experiments show close numerical agreement between interpreted and directly compiled paths, exact-gradient calibration of fixed program structures, and strong amortization through batching.

paper_core_claims.claim: A single bare compiled interpreter can accept distinct Scheme programs as runtime data without per-program recompilation, demonstrated at scale in Experiment J.

Program-and-parameter co-search can recover a synthetic battery structure and produce competitive real-data forecasts, while FluZoo demonstrates that an underconverged inner fitness can erase apparent gains.

function_concept_used_by_paper: A function is an executable Scheme program or closure whose discrete structure is supplied as symbolic data and whose continuous constants are bound as differentiable tensors. The compiler can produce either a program-specific graph or one compiled evaluator that interprets arbitrary program data. Functions therefore have source, graph, artifact, environment, execution trace and gradient behavior, but the paper does not define a governed cross-system function identity or lifecycle.
representation_or_carrier: Scheme source is parsed to an AST, transformed to ANF and lowered to a typed-by-convention ComputeGraph. Runtime values use a 14-component tagged carrier: ten one-hot type slots plus four payload slots. Lists, pairs, closures and environments are heap objects in a write-once Python dictionary addressed by detached integers; numeric/vector/matrix payloads remain tensors. Serialized .ncg graphs are concrete artifacts. Type tags and addresses are discrete routing data, while learnable numeric payloads retain autograd chains.
specification_language: The accepted language is a substantial pure Scheme subset with variables, constants, lambda/application, let/letrec, define, begin, quote, cond/if, closures, first-class functions, general and tail recursion, pairs/lists, comparisons, transcendental functions and vector/matrix primitives. Free-variable names define the binding contract and a supported-operator prescan rejects unknown heads. The language excludes call/cc, set!, mutation and exact-integer semantics, and it has no static effect/capability declarations, pre/postconditions, uncertainty contracts, resource budgets or version constraints.
compiler_or_generator: The shared compiler performs parsing, macro expansion, ANF conversion and ComputeGraph construction, then evaluates graphs through backend-specific tensor operations. Direct mode compiles each scientific program; meta-circular mode compiles evaluator source. Two distinct APIs matter: compile_dmci bakes one quoted object program into its graph, while compile_interpreter leaves program and environment as runtime inputs and can be serialized once. The paper's central reusable-artifact claim is implemented by the latter, but Experiments A-C and multiple other harnesses use program-specific compile_program/compile_dmci caches, so their results do not themselves demonstrate zero recompilation across distinct programs.
interpreter_or_runtime: The 288-line Scheme evaluator performs association-list environment lookup, special-form dispatch, closure application, recursive evaluation and 52 primitive operations. A four-level tail-call strategy and lazy branch evaluation avoid divergent eager expansion and Python-stack growth for supported tail recursion. PyTorch define-by-run supplies reverse-mode AD over the realized trace. Scalar straight-line direct graphs also run on JAX, NumPy and CuPy, but the heap-using, data-dependent meta-circular interpreter is differentiable only on PyTorch in this release.
composition_rule: Scheme application, closures, letrec, list construction, sequential forms, recursion and higher-order calls compose programs through the evaluator; serialized interpreter artifacts can route many program datums through one runtime. The composition proof sketch uses omega-PAP closure on open full-measure trace regions. Operational composition is concrete, but compatibility is enforced mainly by parsing, free-variable bindings and an operator allowlist rather than static types, effect contracts, semantic adapters or governed admission receipts.
state_or_effect_model: Internal state comprises environments, immutable/write-once heap cells, tagged payloads, runtime inputs and recursive control. The pure subset intentionally excludes mutation so stored tensors preserve autograd version chains. The evaluator has no external filesystem, network, device-authority, transaction, compensation, idempotence, rollback or concurrency semantics. Experiment orchestration, LLM calls and data loading occur in host Python outside the formal language and are not covered by the correctness argument.
uncertainty_model: The compiler and gradients are deterministic conditional on code, tensor values, backend order and realized trace; stochasticity enters initialization, optimizers, LLM proposals, search islands and datasets. The released result files and aggregators improve auditability, and several studies report multiple seeds, but confidence intervals are sparse, some major claims rely on three seeds or one hardware run, and no calibrated epistemic/aleatoric function semantics are defined. Trace-boundary uncertainty is a mathematical exceptional-set qualification, not a calibrated probability. Model-selection reuse of held-out data further prevents treating displayed held-out scores as unbiased uncertainty estimates.

validation_regime.bare_interpreter: integration tests exercise compile_interpreter, serialization and multiple runtime programs; Experiment J explicitly uses one interpreter plus evaluate_program, reports 0.02-second one-time compile, and tests 10000 synthetic and 260 LLM-authored programs
validation_regime.compile_path_boundary: Experiments A-C use program-specific sources compiled/cached per model; LIM-ENSO and FluZoo use compile_dmci, which bakes one program. The reusable bare-interpreter path is therefore real but should not be retroactively attributed to every experiment
validation_regime.performance: sequential DMCI is about 14x per evaluation in decomposition, 19x direct in A, 73x direct and 248x hand-coded in B, 74-158x direct in C and 25.3x in D with no crossover. Batching yields large speedups relative to sequential DMCI, while jax.vmap of direct graphs remains faster where applicable: geometric-mean DMCI forward 0.27x and train 0.076x
validation_regime.search: Experiment E finds the discrete operator pair in 26/240 DMCI restarts versus 240/240 exhaustive, 199/240 evolutionary and 5/240 random; DMCI is about 57000x slower than exhaustive and uniquely receives an extra derivative-matching loss term
validation_regime.llm_and_composition: Experiment F reports 11/12 successful runs only after reasoning plus optimizer portfolio; G tests three small composition targets and one remains structurally ambiguous. These are bounded workflow demonstrations rather than autonomous scientific discovery validation
validation_regime.enso: released code fits monthly climatology, linear trend, three-month smoothing, area weights, economy SVD/EOF basis and PC scaling on the full 1950-2024 record before using 1950-1979 for fit and 1980-1989 for held-out scoring. It also chooses optimizer/model portfolios on that held-out skill, with no independent final test; the displayed forecast result is therefore leakage-affected and selection-conditional
validation_regime.battery: synthetic mechanism recovery is anchored by algebraic identity and rigorous rescoring. Real cells are resampled over their full observed lifetime to a 100-point life-fraction grid before early/late splitting, so the coordinate of an early observation depends on future total life; the same cell tails guide search/selection and reported scores, with no independent held-out cells. The result is a conditional retrospective curve-completion score, not a clean deployable early-life forecast
validation_regime.fluzoo: rigorous 300-step rescoring erases the cheap-fitness evolved advantage and ties the SEIR reference, directly documenting inner-objective overfitting

equivalence_notions.boundary: Branch boundaries, degenerate predicates, trace changes, nontermination and parameters used only in conditions are excluded; S3 confirms zero-gradient failure.

lifecycle_and_provenance: The repository supplies source files, Git revisions/tags, an MIT license, .ncg serialization, LFS-backed result artifacts, manifests and experiment-specific READMEs. This is materially stronger provenance than paper-only work. It still lacks content hashes in result manifests, a lockfile/container digest, signed releases, immutable data/model/service identities, formal admission/approval records, deployment telemetry, compatibility migrations, deprecation, rollback policy and tombstones. The four-commit history and post-submission public code also leave no exact pre-submission implementation snapshot.
limitations_and_failure_boundaries: The paper's central compile-once path exists, but compile_dmci bakes one program and Experiments A-C compile/cache a distinct evaluator-plus-program graph per model; only compile_interpreter/evaluate_program provides literal cross-program reuse.
The almost-everywhere theory is a conventional proof sketch, not mechanized proof, and is scoped to terminating trace-constant regions with generic nondegenerate predicates.
Parameters that affect only discrete branch predicates receive zero gradients almost everywhere; S3 converges 0/10 and cannot learn its threshold.
sqrt and log clamps define modified runtime semantics in their clamped regions; correctness applies to the implemented functions rather than ideal mathematical primitives.
The pure subset excludes call/cc, set!, mutation and exact integers; external effects and authority are outside the model.
The differentiable heap-using interpreter is PyTorch-only; JAX support is limited to suitable direct graphs and a fixed-length rewrite is future work.
Unknown evaluator operators historically fall through to a zero-like value, so correctness depends on the host-side supported-operator prescan; bypassing it risks silent corruption.
Sequential interpretation is consistently much slower than direct compilation or hand code, and structural search Experiment D shows no wall-clock crossover.
Batching speedups are measured primarily against DMCI's own sequential execution; direct jax.vmap remains substantially faster where it covers the program.
torch.compile is slower for every reported batched model, so it does not remove current graph-walk latency.
Experiment A uses self-generated noiseless training data with no held-out split; trajectory agreement demonstrates implementation fidelity, not scientific-model correctness.

Experiment B's 15/15 generation follows iterative prompt refinement on a fixed task set, with ten first-order tasks, four recursive/iterative tasks and one closure/composition task; it is not open-ended synthesis.
The paper's 1225-test claim and README's 823-test-function/30-module claim both disagree with audited v1.1/v1.0 code: 1103 passed, 13 skipped, 918 functions and 33 modules.
Requirements specify lower bounds and comments rather than a dependency lock, so the environment is not actually pinned.
The manifest checker validates filenames and counts, not artifact hashes or content integrity, despite broader reproducibility language.
Complete long-running OpenEvolve island archives are not committed; released winners, accepted caches and summaries cannot reconstruct every proposal/selection event.

Experiment E's DMCI discrete recovery is 10.8 percent, far below exhaustive and evolutionary baselines, about 57000 times slower than exhaustive, and benefits from a derivative loss unavailable to comparators.
Experiment I uses three seeds; beyond six parameters no method reaches the stated 1e-3 threshold, so high-dimensional results are relative robustness comparisons rather than recovery demonstrations.

Experiment J's B2 recursive coverage counts hand-port feasibility/LOC even where no executable generated JAX port or recovery measurement exists; engineering-burden totals are proxies, not observed human effort.
Experiment J's LLM hard-recursive parameter recovery is effectively unsuccessful for DMCI despite 100-percent execution coverage; coverage is not optimization success.

LIM-ENSO full-record climatology, detrending, EOF basis and normalization use future data before the train/held-out split, and the same held-out window selects optimizers/structures; the forecast score is not an independent generalization estimate.

Battery real-data life-fraction normalization requires each cell's eventual life endpoint; early-window inputs therefore encode future lifetime information and are not deployable early-life observations.

Battery structure search, selection and headline scoring reuse tails from the same 117 cells with no independent held-out cells; real-data claims support retrospective conditional curve completion only.

The battery synthetic recovery is more credible than the real-data forecast because the data-generating mechanism is known and the recovered structure is checked algebraically after rigorous rescoring.
FluZoo's search-time win disappears under converged rescoring, showing that program-and-parameter co-search can optimize an underfit inner proxy rather than real skill.
Several major measurements are repository self-checks on released artifacts, not clean reruns from raw external inputs or independent empirical validation.
No static effect/capability system, external transaction model, compensation, rollback or governed versioned function registry is provided.
This model review and local code/test audit do not prove the theorems, independently reproduce all experiments or empirically validate ignition.
what_the_paper_does_not_support: It does not establish mechanized compiler, interpreter or gradient correctness.
It does not establish gradient learnability across branch choices or discrete program structure.
It does not establish that every reported DMCI experiment used one frozen cross-program interpreter; several compile a program-specific graph.
It does not establish a general speed advantage over direct compilation, JAX vectorization or exhaustive search.
It does not establish clean out-of-sample ENSO skill because preprocessing and selection cross the stated held-out boundary.
It does not establish deployable early-life battery forecasting because full lifetime determines the input grid and the same cell tails drive selection.
It does not establish autonomous scientific discovery; LLM and co-search outcomes depend on constrained languages, repaired prompts, optimizer portfolios and converged inner objectives.
It does not provide a fully pinned environment, content-hashed artifact manifest, complete search history or signed release provenance.
It does not model external effects, permissions, transactions, compensation or rollback.
It does not define calibrated stochastic function semantics or a governed lifecycle registry.
The model review is not proof or independent empirical validation of the authors' experiments.

GAP-015.reason: The pure Scheme subset, explicit bindings and supported-operator contract constitute a concrete executable specification language for runtime-supplied programs, bounded by missing static effects and resource contracts.

GAP-016.reason: Parsing, macro expansion, ANF lowering, ComputeGraph generation and evaluator compilation form a released, tested compiler path, with an important distinction between program-baked and bare-interpreter APIs.

GAP-017.reason: Value, gradient and composition correspondence are explicit and tested, but theory is non-mechanized, almost-everywhere and trace-conditional, while held-out scientific validity is contaminated in two real-data studies.

GAP-018.reason: Internal heap/environment/control semantics are precise and mutation is deliberately excluded, but external effects, capabilities, transactions and rollback are absent.

GAP-019.reason: Git tags, serialized .ncg graphs, LFS artifacts, manifests and READMEs provide substantial provenance, but hashes, locked environments, admission/deployment history, migration and rollback lifecycle are incomplete.

GAP-020.reason: Multiple seeds and explicit trace-boundary qualifications expose some uncertainty, but no calibrated stochastic function semantics or uncertainty-aware admission policy is defined.

N1_FunctionSpec.reason: Scheme source, free-variable bindings, pure-language rules and operator allowlists form executable bounded function specifications.

N2_Representation.reason: AST/ANF/ComputeGraph, 14-dimensional tagged values, tensor payloads, closures, environments and detached heap addresses provide explicit carriers.

N3_Compiler.reason: The released parser-to-ANF-to-graph pipeline compiles both object programs and the evaluator itself and is covered by a large passing test suite.

N4_Artifact.reason: Serializable .ncg graphs, code, accepted programs and LFS-backed results are concrete artifacts, though their lifecycle and environment identities remain incomplete.

N5_Interpreter.reason: The released 288-line self-hosted Scheme evaluator plus PyTorch graph engine implements runtime program interpretation and differentiation.

N6_ExecutionTrace.reason: Define-by-run execution realizes program-dependent traces and many per-run outputs are committed, but there is no uniform tamper-evident trace ledger across compiler, LLM and search events.

N7_Validator.reason: Tests, operator prescan, numerical parity gates, manifests and aggregators are concrete validators, but counts conflict, manifests are filename-only and real-data held-out boundaries are compromised.

N8_ComposerRouter.reason: Closures, higher-order application, recursion, runtime program data and one reusable interpreter concretely compose and route functions, without static effect compatibility.

N9_VersionedRegistry.reason: Git tags, files and serialized artifacts provide identifiers and provenance, but no governed admission, usage, compatibility, migration, deprecation or rollback registry exists.

confirmed_projection: The exact paper and released repository directly confirm a bounded FunctionSpec-Representation-Compiler-Artifact-Interpreter-ExecutionTrace-Validator-Composer architecture: a pure Scheme specification is lowered through AST/ANF to a graph, the same compiler builds a self-hosted evaluator, a serialized bare interpreter accepts program/environment data at runtime, tagged heap values preserve tensor gradients, and tests/artifacts validate many paths.
