function_concept_used_by_paper: The central function is an input-conditioned mixture MoE(x)=sum_{i in I_D} w_i M_i(x): a gating function computes scores or probabilities, selects a subset of expert functions, dispatches the input and combines expert outputs. Experts may be FFNs, attention heads, CNNs, adapters, policies or task/domain modules. This is a concrete router-composer architecture, not a low-rank parameter delta, a general function specification language or a weight-space arithmetic algebra.
specification_language: The survey describes task objectives, data domains, learned gate scores, TopK rules, expert capacity, load losses and cited application protocols. These are architecture/training specifications, not a typed callable contract with machine-checkable preconditions, postconditions, effect signatures or authority constraints.
representation_or_carrier: A routed function is carried jointly by expert-network parameters, gating parameters or embeddings, the selected expert-index set, normalized mixture weights and the base architecture in which the MoE layer is embedded. Some cited systems use adapters, masks, prompts, policies or local client models, but the paper does not reduce all experts to one carrier type.
compiler_or_generator: Supervised, reinforcement, meta, continual or federated optimization learns the router and experts; some cited designs add, merge, mask, upcycle or hypernetwork-generate experts. This is model generation and adaptation, not compilation from a declarative FunctionSpec or semantics-preserving lowering.
interpreter_or_runtime: At inference, a router scores an input, a dispatcher sends it to selected experts, expert runtimes evaluate their subnetworks and a combiner forms a weighted output. Distributed deployments add expert/data/model/tensor parallel execution, all-to-all communication, scheduling, caching and memory movement. The survey specifies this pattern but releases no runtime implementation of its own.
state_or_effect_model: Training mutates router/expert parameters and load statistics; runtime produces dispatch, communication, memory, scheduling, capacity-overflow and possible token-drop effects. The surveyed applications also include recurrent, continual, RL and federated state. No unified effect type system, capability boundary, transaction model, compensation semantics or rollback protocol is defined.
composition_rule: Composition is primarily input-conditioned output-space routing: hard TopK or soft gating selects experts and the combiner sums or averages their outputs with weights. Hierarchical/task/modality routers and cited expert-merging designs extend this pattern. This is not generally weight-space addition or merging of independently specified functions, and no associativity, commutativity, identity, compatibility or semantic-preservation law is established.
equivalence_notions: The survey compares cited systems through task-specific accuracy, loss, return, latency, throughput, resource use and theoretical convergence/approximation results. It supplies no cross-carrier equivalence relation, behavioral test suite, distributional tolerance or proof that a routed mixture is equivalent to any dense, merged or symbolic function.

validation_regime.source_type: Narrative technical survey/preprint. It contributes a taxonomy and secondary synthesis, not a new MoE system, dataset, benchmark, experiment, theorem or replication.
validation_regime.review_methodology: No database/search query, search date, inclusion/exclusion criteria, screening flow, duplicate handling, quality appraisal, risk-of-bias assessment or reproducible evidence table is reported. The word 'systematic' describes topical organization, not a documented systematic-review protocol.
validation_regime.coverage: The v4 bibliography contains 305 entries and the roadmap spans basic design, five learning paradigms, theory, CV and NLP. Breadth does not by itself establish completeness, unbiased selection or equal evidentiary quality.
validation_regime.quantitative_synthesis: Headline numbers such as Switch Transformer speedups, DeepSpeed compression, Mixtral active/total parameters and application metrics are inherited from heterogeneous cited studies. The survey performs no metric normalization, hardware/compute matching, meta-analysis, uncertainty aggregation or independent recalculation.
validation_regime.theory_boundary: Section IV summarizes approximation, convergence, identifiability and specialization results from cited papers, mainly for simplified gates/experts. Those proofs are not proofs contributed or mechanically checked by this survey, and the survey explicitly says deep-MoE theory remains elusive.
validation_regime.system_boundary: The paper identifies computation imbalance, all-to-all communication and memory as separate deployment bottlenecks and surveys parallelism, scheduling, caching and low-precision communication; it provides no unified benchmark or audited implementation.
validation_regime.artifact: The authors release the exact manuscript source and bibliography only. A single DeepEP link is a cited third-party implementation; it is not authors' code or a reproduction package for the survey's claims.
validation_regime.editorial_consistency: Sections I and III twice say 'four' learning paradigms/domains while listing five: continual learning, meta-learning, multi-task learning, reinforcement learning and federated learning. The taxonomy itself includes all five, so this is recorded as an unresolved editorial counting error rather than silently corrected.
validation_regime.reproducibility: Document integrity and citation inventory are reproducible from arXiv v4, but the literature-selection process and cross-paper claims cannot be exactly replayed from released artifacts.

uncertainty_model: Softmax, Gaussian/exponential-family, Student-t, multinomial-probit and noisy routing provide probabilistic or stochastic control variables, and cited training uses random exploration/dropout. These quantities govern assignment or robustness; they are not necessarily calibrated epistemic uncertainty. The survey provides no common calibration definition, confidence protocol or uncertainty-aware admission rule across its 305 heterogeneous sources.
lifecycle_and_provenance: The architectural lifecycle is expert initialization or upcycling, joint/specialized training, route selection, dispatch, expert execution, output combination, evaluation and possible expert addition/merging/caching. The paper supplies v1-v4 manuscript history and source hashes through arXiv, but no versioned expert registry, expert/checkpoint identifiers, dependency graph, compatibility contract, approval state, monitoring record, deprecation rule, rollback procedure or tombstone model.

N1_FunctionSpec.reason: Gate equations, capacity/load objectives and task/domain definitions specify bounded routing behavior, but there is no typed pre/post/effect contract for expert functions.

N2_Representation.reason: Experts, gate parameters, expert indices and mixture weights form a concrete distributed representation of an input-conditioned composite neural function.

N3_Compiler.reason: Training, upcycling, expert generation and adaptation produce routed models, but no declarative lowering or semantic-preservation guarantee exists.

N4_Artifact.reason: Cited expert networks, adapters, masks and checkpoints are deployable artifact forms, while this survey releases no governed model artifact or common artifact schema.

N5_Interpreter.reason: Router-dispatch-expert-combine is a concrete runtime pattern with distributed execution concerns, but the paper contributes no executable interpreter or formal operational semantics.

N6_ExecutionTrace.reason: Routing decisions could be logged, yet the survey defines no trace schema and releases no per-token, per-expert or system execution traces.

N7_Validator.reason: The survey catalogs performance, efficiency, theory and robustness criteria, but supplies no unified validator, reproduced measurement or cross-study acceptance threshold.

N8_ComposerRouter.reason: Input-conditioned gating, expert selection, dispatch and weighted output combination are the paper's central architecture and directly instantiate a bounded neural composer/router.

N9_VersionedRegistry.reason: ArXiv versions the manuscript, not expert-function artifacts; no provenance-complete registry, compatibility model or rollback lifecycle is defined.

GAP-015.reason: Routing equations and training objectives are machine-readable fragments, but not a formal function specification language with preconditions, postconditions and effects.

GAP-016.reason: MoE output-space gating and expert selection are not a weight-space composition algebra; the survey defines no parameter-arithmetic laws for combining independent functions.

GAP-017.reason: Task metrics and cited approximation/convergence results do not provide a checker for equivalence across expert, dense, adapter, merged or symbolic representations.

GAP-018.reason: Dispatch, all-to-all communication, capacity overflow, token drop, memory movement and learning-state mutation expose concrete effects without effect signatures or handlers.

GAP-019.reason: The paper surveys expert lifecycle fragments but supplies no machine-readable versioned function registry or provenance/compatibility/rollback protocol.

GAP-020.reason: Probabilistic/noisy gating is explicit, but assignment probabilities are not a formal calibrated stochastic function semantics or uncertainty-governance framework.

source_specific_reasoning: PARTIAL is bounded to the survey's direct documentary support for MoE Representation and ComposerRouter and its useful catalog of compiler/runtime/validator fragments. The exact v4 equations and taxonomy clearly establish expert functions, learned gating, conditional dispatch and output combination. The verdict remains partial because this is secondary narrative evidence with no systematic search protocol, original implementation, experiment, unified validator, execution trace, equivalence checker, effect system or registry. It does not accept the metadata card's wrong authors, low-rank-delta carrier, adapter-forward runtime, stateless-inference claim or adapter-arithmetic composition rule.
confirmed_projection: The exact arXiv v4 survey directly confirms a bounded neural ComposerRouter pattern: a learned gate maps an input to expert scores, dispatches the input to selected expert functions and combines their outputs, while distributed runtime choices expose computation, communication and memory tradeoffs. This supports Function OS representation/routing design only as secondary architecture evidence, not as a released Function OS implementation or validation of ignition.
projection_boundary: These are 121CX projections from the exact 29-page arXiv v4 PDF, every rendered page, complete TeX source and all 305 bibliography entries. Cited empirical and theoretical results were not independently re-executed or re-proved. This model review is not a systematic-review certification, mechanized proof, implementation audit of 305 cited systems, independent empirical validation, or validation of ignition.
what_the_paper_does_not_support: It does not show that all experts are low-rank adapters or that MoE is primarily a low-rank weight-delta method.
It does not define weight-space addition, subtraction, merging or an algebra over independently learned functions.
It does not provide typed preconditions, postconditions, effect signatures or capability boundaries for experts.
It does not prove that routing decisions reflect semantic task identity, causal specialization or human-interpretable knowledge boundaries.
It does not establish equivalence between a sparse MoE and a dense, merged, symbolic or single-expert function.
It does not contribute a general compiler, interpreter, trace format, validator or versioned expert registry.
It does not independently reproduce or statistically synthesize the heterogeneous results of cited studies.
It does not prove the deep-MoE theoretical properties that it explicitly identifies as open.
It does not demonstrate that conditional activation always lowers end-to-end latency, memory, communication or total cost.
This review is not proof or independent empirical validation of the survey's cited claims.
limitations_and_failure_boundaries: The paper is an arXiv preprint whose v4 states that it has been submitted to IEEE; no completed peer-review status is established by the source.
The survey reports no reproducible literature-search or study-selection protocol, so completeness and selection bias cannot be assessed.
There is no inclusion/exclusion criterion, screening flow, quality assessment, risk-of-bias analysis or evidence-grading framework.
The paper makes broad performance/efficiency statements using heterogeneous cited studies without common hardware, compute, data, metrics or uncertainty normalization.
The source archive contains manuscript materials only and no author implementation, datasets, checkpoints, logs or result-generation scripts.
A third-party DeepEP repository link is not a released implementation of this survey or a reproduction package for its claims.
The introduction and algorithm section call five listed learning paradigms 'four', an unresolved internal counting inconsistency.
The historical metadata card misattributes the authors as Cai et al.; the official arXiv record and manuscript name Siyuan Mu and Sen Lin.
The historical metadata card assigns a generic low-rank adapter template that does not match this paper's MoE subject or equations.
Hard TopK may exclude useful experts and is non-smooth; soft routing avoids discrete allocation but can increase computation and blur specialization.
Uneven routing can cause expert underuse, insufficient specialization, token dropping and model collapse; auxiliary losses and capacities add tuning tradeoffs.
Sparse activation reduces activated compute but total parameters still impose storage, communication, memory and scheduling costs.
Expert parallelism can create non-uniform workloads, synchronization delay and all-to-all communication bottlenecks.
Dynamic expert selection creates complex memory-access patterns and can exceed a single device's storage capacity.
Expert specialization and router decisions are not automatically interpretable; the paper lists interpretability/theory as open research.
Section IV's theory is dominated by simplified gates/experts and selected tasks; the survey states deep neural MoE understanding remains elusive.
Application summaries often repeat author-reported superiority language without independent replication or common statistical criteria.
Federated-learning discussion does not establish privacy, security or fairness merely from keeping data local; those properties require separate threat models and validation.
Routing probabilities and noisy gates are operational assignment mechanisms, not calibrated uncertainty estimates.
No source-level semantics, effect handling, cross-representation equivalence or learned-artifact lifecycle governance is supplied.
This audit verifies document integrity and performs semantic review; it does not audit all 305 cited papers or validate their measurements.

paper_core_claims.claim: NeuPSL Deep Weights replaces a single shared symbolic rule weight with neural-network outputs that can specialize the weight of each grounded rule instance from its atom features.
For fixed non-negative neural/symbolic weights, the resulting deep HL-MRF retains convex symbolic MAP inference while gradient-based learning updates neural and symbolic parameters.
On the authors' synthetic existing-community graph task, Deep Weights improves over evaluated MLP, GraphSAGE and shared-weight PSL baselines in high-signal and most moderate-noise settings.
Supervised-only training and synthetic-only evaluation limit conclusions about latent variables and real-world applicability.

function_concept_used_by_paper: A NeuPSL function is a declarative soft-logic program grounded into hinge-loss potentials and linear constraints. Neural predicates map raw features to atom truth values, while Deep Weights networks map the features of all atoms in a grounded rule to a non-negative scalar importance weight. The resulting energy is a weighted sum of grounded potential functions and MAP inference returns the target assignment. These are neural-generated rule weights, not neural-network weights treated as complete programs or a general weight-space computation algebra.
specification_language: PSL supplies first-order logical clauses, linear arithmetic rules, observed/unobserved atoms, categorical simplex constraints and continuous Łukasiewicz relaxations. It is a real declarative relational specification language for this bounded runtime, but the paper does not add general precondition/postcondition/effect/capability contracts.
representation_or_carrier: The executable carrier combines a PSL rule template, grounded atoms, an ordered partition of hinge-loss potentials, non-negative shared symbolic weights, neural predicate parameters, instance-specific Deep Weights MLP parameters, linear constraints and the resulting deep HL-MRF energy/distribution.
compiler_or_generator: Grounding substitutes constants for variables and lowers logical/arithmetic rules into convex hinge-loss potentials and constraints. Deep Weights MLPs generate scalar weights for each instantiated potential from rule-atom features, and supervised backpropagation learns both neural and symbolic parameters.
interpreter_or_runtime: Neural inference evaluates deep predicates and Deep Weights networks. Symbolic inference then minimizes the deep HL-MRF energy over the constrained [0,1] target domain. The optimization is convex and globally solvable only conditional on fixed neural outputs/non-negative weights and the paper's linear/hinge-loss construction; end-to-end neural learning is not claimed convex.
state_or_effect_model: Training mutates neural and symbolic parameters; inference reads observed atoms/features and produces target atom assignments through a constrained optimizer. The paper models no external I/O, capabilities, exceptions, authority, transactions, compensation or rollback, and it does not define effects for rule grounding or optimization failure.
composition_rule: Grounded rule potentials compose additively inside an energy, multiplied by shared symbolic or instance-specific neural scalar weights, while unweighted rules impose hard linear constraints. This is potential/constraint composition, not addition, interpolation or merging of complete neural function parameter vectors.
equivalence_notions: Categorical accuracy on five synthetic splits compares outputs of MLP, GNN, shared-weight PSL and Deep Weights models. No semantic equivalence relation is defined between programs, groundings, parameterizations or neural/symbolic representations; finite mean accuracy is not equivalence.

validation_regime.formal: Definition 3.1 gives the deep HL-MRF energy, conditional Gibbs density, feasible set and empirical-risk derivatives. Convexity/global-optimum language applies to fixed-weight symbolic MAP inference. No theorem establishes learning convergence, generalization, rule recovery, identifiability or semantic equivalence.
validation_regime.dataset: Twenty-five disjoint fully connected communities, four labels, 10-15 nodes per community and two generator rules. RuleFeatures communities encode labels in features; RuleCommunity communities share one label and require existing-community propagation. Test nodes are new nodes in communities already represented by at least two training nodes, not unseen-community or new-rule transfer.
validation_regime.generator_contradiction: The paper sets k=25 total communities and also says equal numbers are generated from the two mutually exclusive rule families. An odd total cannot be divided equally, and no released generator resolves the actual 12/13 allocation.
validation_regime.splits: Five splits with 60/30/10 train/test/validation partitions are reported. Means and standard deviations are across the five splits; seed identities, split files and per-split predictions are not released.
validation_regime.hyperparameters: Appendix Tables 3-4 list tuning ranges and final values, sometimes separately for every covariance setting. The search algorithm, validation objective, tie-breaking, number of trials and whether selection was nested away from test data are not described.
validation_regime.high_signal_results: At the highest-correlation settings, Deep Weights reports 100.00+-0.00, 100.00+-0.00 and 93.35+-2.23 percent for OH+OH, G+OH and G+G, compared with MLP 99.09/88.10/89.04, GNN 98.43/94.56/81.75 and PSL 81.07/87.06/86.71 percent.
validation_regime.noise_sweep: At G+OH covariance 100, Deep Weights falls to 62.44+-5.70 versus MLP 69.70+-3.22 and PSL 69.47+-5.06. At G+G covariance 50 PSL is 74.18+-4.91 versus Deep Weights 72.57+-6.58; at covariance 100 PSL is 69.39+-5.09 and GNN 54.14+-6.19 versus Deep Weights 51.66+-6.89. The method is not uniformly best.
validation_regime.benchmark_alignment: The synthetic graph is generated by the same two feature/label-propagation structures that the PSL/Deep Weights rules encode. This is a controlled capability test, not evidence of discovering unknown real-world symbolic structure.
validation_regime.uncertainty_statistics: Standard deviations over five splits are supplied, but no confidence intervals, paired tests, effect sizes, multiple-comparison correction or raw predictions are released. Overlapping standard deviations are discussed informally rather than tested.
validation_regime.hardware: Only an Ubuntu 22.04.1 CPU machine with Intel Xeon E5-2630 v4 at 3.10 GHz is reported. No wall time, memory, scaling, energy or comparison-cost measurement is provided.
validation_regime.artifact: The footnote promises public code/data upon acceptance, but no dedicated Deep Weights artifact was identified. The closest LINQS NeuPSL repository is for a different IJCAI paper and does not contain this dataset or method.
validation_regime.reproducibility: Equations, generator prose and hyperparameter tables are substantial, but the unresolved 25/equal contradiction and missing code, data, seeds, split files, raw outputs, environment and result scripts prevent exact reproduction.

uncertainty_model: The model defines an explicit conditional Gibbs density over target atoms using a deep HL-MRF energy, with atom values in [0,1], then performs MAP inference. This is genuine probabilistic/soft semantics for a finite constrained model, though the evaluated outputs are point estimates. The paper provides no calibration, posterior uncertainty, predictive interval or epistemic treatment for neural-generated rule weights.
lifecycle_and_provenance: The conceptual lifecycle is author-written PSL templates, grounding, neural predicate/deep-weight initialization, hyperparameter search, supervised learning, fixed-weight MAP inference and synthetic evaluation. The immutable paper PDF and official workshop metadata are identifiable, but no KLR code/data release, model checkpoint, configuration receipt, seed/split manifest, learned-rule-weight artifact, compatibility record, monitoring, deprecation, migration or rollback lifecycle is public.

N1_FunctionSpec.reason: PSL clauses, arithmetic rules, atom domains and hard constraints provide a concrete bounded declarative specification for relational target functions.

N2_Representation.reason: Rules, grounded potentials, constraints, neural predicates and instance-specific neural rule weights form an explicit hybrid symbolic-neural carrier.

N3_Compiler.reason: Grounding lowers templates to hinge-loss potentials/constraints and Deep Weights networks generate executable per-grounding scalar parameters.

N4_Artifact.reason: A learned PSL program and neural checkpoints are concrete artifact forms, but the promised Deep Weights code, data, checkpoints and receipts were not identified.

N5_Interpreter.reason: Neural evaluation followed by constrained convex MAP energy minimization is a fully specified bounded interpreter/runtime for the grounded model.

N6_ExecutionTrace.reason: Potential values and optimizer states could be traced, but the paper defines no trace schema and releases no inference or learning traces.

N7_Validator.reason: Five-split synthetic categorical accuracy is a bounded behavioral validator, not semantic, calibration, safety or real-world validation.

N8_ComposerRouter.reason: Weighted energy terms and constraints compose grounded rules, but there is no router or semantic composition of independently packaged callable functions.

N9_VersionedRegistry.reason: No versioned learned-program registry, dependency graph, compatibility model or rollback lifecycle is defined or released.

GAP-015.reason: PSL is a genuine logical/arithmetic specification language with constraints, but it does not supply general function preconditions, postconditions and effect signatures.

GAP-016.reason: The learned deep weights are scalar importance weights on grounded potentials, not complete program parameters and not a weight-space algebra for combining functions.

GAP-017.reason: Synthetic accuracy comparisons do not check equivalence across symbolic programs, neural networks or alternate carriers.

GAP-018.reason: The paper models constrained internal inference/training but contributes no language-level effect signatures, handlers, capabilities or rollback.

GAP-019.reason: No code/data release or versioned learned-function registry with provenance, compatibility and rollback is supplied.

GAP-020.reason: The deep HL-MRF defines an explicit finite conditional probability density and MAP semantics, providing bounded probabilistic function semantics even though calibration is not evaluated.

source_specific_reasoning: CONFIRMED is bounded to the paper's explicit hybrid FunctionSpec-Representation-Compiler-Interpreter architecture. The exact equations directly connect declarative PSL rules, grounded convex potentials, neural predicates, instance-specific learned rule weights and constrained MAP execution. Confirmation does not extend to the historical metadata card's weights-as-program or weight-arithmetic framing, to uniform empirical superiority, to real-world generalization, or to artifact reproducibility. The odd-community contradiction, high-noise losses, existing-community benchmark design, workshop venue and unfulfilled code/data footnote remain explicit boundaries.
confirmed_projection: The exact workshop paper confirms a bounded neural-symbolic FunctionSpec-Representation-Compiler-Interpreter path: logical/arithmetic rules are grounded into convex potentials and constraints, neural networks generate atom values and per-grounding scalar rule weights, and constrained MAP inference executes the combined energy model. This is strong architecture evidence for learned parameterization inside a symbolic runtime, not evidence that neural weight space itself is a program algebra.
projection_boundary: These are 121CX projections from the exact author-hosted 11-page paper, every rendered page, the official ICML KLR poster record, LINQS metadata and a bounded public-artifact search. The synthetic experiments were not rerun and no dedicated artifact was available to audit. This model review is not a mechanized proof, independent empirical validation, real-world validation, code-release certification or validation of ignition.
what_the_paper_does_not_support: It does not treat an entire neural parameter vector as a symbolic program or establish weight space as program space.
It does not define arithmetic for adding, subtracting, merging or composing independently learned neural functions.
It does not learn symbolic rule structures; the modeler supplies the two PSL rules and neural networks specialize their grounded scalar weights.
It does not prove end-to-end neural training is convex or globally optimal; convexity applies to fixed-weight symbolic MAP inference.
It does not prove learned deep weights recover true communities, causal rules or human-interpretable symbolic structure.
It does not establish semantic equivalence between Deep Weights, PSL, GNN or MLP representations.
It does not demonstrate uniform superiority across the covariance sweep.
It does not validate unsupervised latent variables, unseen communities, unseen rule structures or real-world data.
It does not provide external effect semantics, execution traces or a versioned artifact registry.
This review is not proof or independent empirical validation of the reported experiments.
limitations_and_failure_boundaries: The frozen title omits the word 'Soft'; the exact paper and official records use Neural Probabilistic Soft Logic.
The frozen metadata card misattributes the first author as Pryor, H.; the paper names Connor Pryor, Charles Dickens and Lise Getoor.
The frozen metadata card calls the source an arXiv preprint and supplies a generic weights-as-program template; official records classify it as a KLR workshop poster.
The PDF contains ICML/PMLR main-proceedings boilerplate, while the official ICML event and author publication records identify a workshop poster; the latter controls venue classification.
The paper's footnote promises code/data after acceptance, but no dedicated Deep Weights repository, dataset or experiment release was identified.
The public neupsl-ijcai23 repository is for a different paper and cannot be used as evidence that this method or dataset was released.
Exactly 25 communities cannot be divided into equal counts of the two mutually exclusive generator rule types, contradicting the experiment prose.
No released generator resolves whether the actual split was 12/13, 13/12 or something else.
The inductive experiment adds test nodes to existing communities that each have at least two training nodes; it is not unseen-community generalization.
One-hot community features can directly identify existing community membership, and RuleFeatures data encode labels in features by construction.
The generator and evaluated PSL rules are intentionally aligned, so performance demonstrates use of supplied structure rather than discovery of unknown symbolic rules.
Only five splits are reported, without seed IDs, raw per-split predictions, confidence intervals or significance tests.
The hyperparameter selection algorithm, validation metric, tie-breaking and separation from test inspection are not described.
Deep Weights is not uniformly best: shared PSL is materially stronger at the noisiest G+G setting and also wins other high-noise comparisons.
Standard-deviation overlap is used rhetorically without a paired statistical test.
All evidence is synthetic; the authors explicitly defer real-world applications.
Training is supervised only and the authors explicitly identify unsupervised latent variables as unsupported.
The only hardware receipt is a CPU model/OS; no runtime, memory, scaling or resource comparison is reported.
MAP point predictions do not evaluate probability calibration or neural-rule-weight uncertainty.
Convex symbolic inference relies on non-negative weights, hinge-loss potentials and linear constraints and does not generalize automatically to arbitrary rules or neural learners.
No checkpoints, environment lock, split manifest, result logs or provenance-complete learned-program artifacts are public.
This audit verifies the document and public-artifact boundary; it does not reproduce the five-split measurements.

paper_core_claims.claim: For the evaluated four-convolution MAML classifiers, freezing the entire network body during test-time inner adaptation causes only a modest accuracy change, while body activations remain highly similar by CCA/CKA.
ANIL removes inner-loop updates from the body during both training and testing but retains task-specific gradient adaptation of the head and outer-loop meta-gradients through that adaptation.
paper_core_claims.anchors: section 4, Figure 4, ANIL equation and appendix C.1 equations 1-10

paper_core_claims.claim: Across three initializations, ANIL reports broadly comparable point performance to MAML on Omniglot, MiniImageNet and three simulated RL benchmarks, with lower measured iteration time on one Titan-Xp setup.
After MAML/ANIL training, NIL can discard the learned head at test time and classify with cosine similarity between frozen body representations and support examples.
The authors explicitly restrict their study mainly to benchmark datasets and leave other few-shot distributions for future work.

function_concept_used_by_paper: The paper treats a neural network as a body feature function plus a task-specific classification or policy head. Meta-training learns a reusable body and head initialization. ANIL generates per-task head parameters from support data through gradient descent while leaving body parameters fixed in the inner loop; NIL reuses the body directly and constructs test predictions from cosine similarity to support representations. This is localized task adaptation, not a low-rank adapter, task-description-to-delta generator, arbitrary function compiler or weight-space composition algebra.
specification_language: A task is represented implicitly by a distribution over support and target examples or trajectories, a loss/return objective, way/shot counts, model architecture and update hyperparameters. This is a mathematical learning-task specification, not a typed FunctionSpec with named inputs/outputs, preconditions, postconditions, effects, authority, failure semantics, resource budgets or version constraints.

representation_or_carrier.shared_carrier: meta-trained body parameters and a head initialization
representation_or_carrier.anil_task_carrier: ephemeral task-specific head parameters produced by inner-loop gradient steps; body parameters are shared unchanged within each task adaptation
representation_or_carrier.nil_task_carrier: frozen body representations of support examples, their labels and cosine similarities; the trained head is removed at test time
representation_or_carrier.analysis_carrier: layer activations before/after adaptation and complete parameter vectors used for CCA, CKA and Euclidean comparisons
representation_or_carrier.explicit_non_lora_boundary: The paper uses ordinary dense convolutional/MLP parameters and a full dense final head. It defines no rank factorization, adapter module, delta checkpoint format or learned task-description-to-adapter generator.

compiler_or_generator.outer_process: Meta-optimize the shared body/head initialization from target losses across tasks, differentiating through support-set head adaptation in ANIL.
compiler_or_generator.anil_inner_process: For each task, keep body parameters fixed and update only the final-layer/head parameters by one or more support-loss gradient steps.
compiler_or_generator.nil_process: At test time, discard the head, embed labelled support and query items with the frozen body, and weight support labels by representation similarity.
compiler_or_generator.classification: ANIL is a concrete bounded task-to-head weight generator and a training-time partial-update rule. It is only a compiler analogy because task intent is implicit in samples, no declarative contract is lowered, and no semantic-preservation guarantee is supplied.

interpreter_or_runtime: Execution is an ordinary neural forward pass under the fixed body and adapted head, or a body embedding plus cosine-similarity classifier in NIL. The paper defines no instruction language, evaluator for independently represented functions, effect handler, capability model, exception contract or general function runtime.
state_or_effect_model: Training mutates shared parameters and ANIL task adaptation creates ephemeral head state; RL interacts with simulated environments through trajectories and stochastic policies. These are learning and environment states, not language-level effects: there are no effect signatures, capabilities, transaction boundaries, idempotence rules, compensation, rollback or external-action safety model.
composition_rule: ANIL structurally attaches one adapted head to one shared body and composes gradient operations over time. NIL combines cosine similarities with support labels. Neither operation combines independently versioned callable functions or parameter deltas, and no addition, interpolation, merge compatibility, router or algebraic law is defined.

equivalence_notions.support: MAML, ANIL and NIL point estimates are compared by mean accuracy or average return across three initializations.
equivalence_notions.boundary: The paper reports standard deviations but no equivalence margin, hypothesis test or confidence interval. Several point estimates differ materially, so 'identical' or 'matches' is an empirical shorthand, not statistical or semantic equivalence.

equivalence_notions.support: CCA and CKA compare pre/post-adaptation body activations and MAML/ANIL representations across seeds.
equivalence_notions.boundary: High CCA/CKA indicates similarity under those metrics and sampled inputs; it does not prove equal functions, equal outputs on all inputs, equal parameters or semantic substitutability.

equivalence_notions.support: MiniImageNet accuracy is measured while freezing increasingly many body layers during test adaptation.
equivalence_notions.boundary: A modest benchmark accuracy change does not prove body updates are universally unnecessary, and freezing all four layers changes reported 5-shot accuracy from 63.1+-0.4 to 61.0+-0.6.

equivalence_notions.support: Training and validation loss/accuracy curves for ANIL and MAML visually track one another.
equivalence_notions.boundary: Visual curve similarity without released run data is not trace equivalence or independent reproduction.

validation_regime.formal: The paper writes the MAML/ANIL objectives and a two-layer derivation showing that ANIL removes the body inner update but retains second-order terms through head adaptation. It gives no theorem proving feature reuse, performance equivalence, convergence, generalization or semantic preservation.
validation_regime.freezing: On MiniImageNet 5-way, no freezing reports 46.9+-0.2 1-shot and 63.1+-0.4 5-shot; freezing all four body layers reports 46.3+-0.4 and 61.0+-0.6. Results are averaged over three seeds. The drop is described as small, not formally tested for equivalence.
validation_regime.representation_analysis: CCA/CKA on activations before and after inner adaptation, cross-seed controls and Euclidean weight distances all support limited body change in the evaluated shallow networks. The authors themselves note Euclidean distance is a weaker proxy for functional change.
validation_regime.classification: Table 2 reports MAML versus ANIL as 93.7+-0.7 versus 96.2+-0.5 and 96.4+-0.1 versus 98.0+-0.3 on Omniglot 20-way 1-/5-shot, and 46.9+-0.2 versus 46.7+-0.4 and 63.1+-0.4 versus 61.5+-0.5 on MiniImageNet 5-way 1-/5-shot. Means and standard deviations are over only three random initializations.
validation_regime.nil: NIL reports 96.7+-0.3, 98.0+-0.04, 48.0+-0.7 and 62.2+-0.5 on the four classification tasks, showing that a cosine classifier over learned features is competitive in this protocol, not that a head is irrelevant for all tasks.
validation_regime.reinforcement_learning: Three MAML and three ANIL initializations are evaluated on HalfCheetah-Direction, HalfCheetah-Velocity and 2D-Navigation. The authors disclose that their MAML results do not match the original paper and may have large initialization variance. They select the best-performing model over 500 training iterations and then test it on new tasks, without a separately specified validation selection rule.
validation_regime.timing: Forward/backward timing uses one TensorFlow implementation on a single NVIDIA Titan-Xp, task batch size 1, target set size 1, preloaded images and 2,000 batches. Reported average summary speedups are about 1.7x per training iteration and 4.1x per inference iteration. This excludes data loading and is not a systems-level throughput, memory or energy evaluation.
validation_regime.dataset_protocol_ambiguity: Appendix A says MiniImageNet has 64 training, 12 validation and 24 test classes, but describes the test-time task as drawing randomly chosen validation classes. With no released ANIL split/run artifact, whether this wording is a typo or the actual evaluation split cannot be resolved from the paper package.
validation_regime.artifact: The paper specifies architectures and central hyperparameters, but supplies no ANIL/NIL code, dependency environment, exact seeds, checkpoints, raw curves, timing logs, task/split manifest or result script. The two linked repositories implement baseline MAML rather than the reviewed modification.
validation_regime.reproducibility: Document-level reconstruction is possible, but exact result reproduction is not established because the method patch and paper-run receipts are absent, the baseline frameworks are old, RL results are selection-sensitive and the MiniImageNet split wording is ambiguous.

uncertainty_model: Tasks, support/query samples, random initialization, trajectories and stochastic policies are probabilistic sources. Reported values use mean plus standard deviation across three initializations, while representation plots also average over tasks/repeats. No seed identities, raw per-run values, confidence intervals, equivalence tests, calibrated predictive uncertainty, posterior semantics or propagation of best-iterate/model-selection uncertainty is provided.
lifecycle_and_provenance: The conceptual lifecycle is meta-training, shared body/head initialization, per-task ephemeral head adaptation, target evaluation and optional NIL head removal. The exact PDF/source are identifiable, but no released ANIL checkpoint or immutable method code binds reported results to a repository state. The linked supervised and RL repositories are baseline dependencies, not provenance-complete derived artifacts. No registry records body/head compatibility, dataset/split identity, lineage, approval, deployment, monitoring, deprecation, migration or rollback.

N1_FunctionSpec.reason: Task distributions, support/query sets, objectives and way/shot protocols specify bounded learning problems, but not typed callable contracts with pre/postconditions and effects.

N2_Representation.reason: A reusable body plus an ephemeral task-adapted dense head is an explicit neural function carrier, and NIL supplies a second body-representation-plus-support-set carrier.

N3_Compiler.reason: Outer meta-learning plus head-only inner gradients concretely generates task-specific weights from support data, but no declarative specification is lowered and no semantic guarantee is given.

N4_Artifact.reason: Shared body/checkpoint and adapted head are natural artifacts, but the paper releases neither ANIL/NIL code nor paper-run checkpoints, configurations or immutable receipts.

N5_Interpreter.reason: A standard network forward pass or cosine classifier is an execution mechanism, not an interpreter for a function language or independently packaged function representation.

N6_ExecutionTrace.reason: Learning curves and representation probes are aggregate analyses; no per-task adaptation/execution trace schema or replayable trace artifact is defined.

N7_Validator.reason: Held-out accuracy, return, layer-freezing ablations, representation metrics and timing provide bounded empirical checks without equivalence, safety or semantic validation.

N8_ComposerRouter.reason: Attaching one task head to one shared body and weighting labels by cosine similarity do not compose or route among independently versioned callable functions.

N9_VersionedRegistry.reason: No versioned registry, lineage manifest, compatibility rule, rollout state or rollback protocol for bodies, heads, tasks or checkpoints is defined.

GAP-015.reason: The task objective and support/query protocol are useful mathematical specification fragments but omit machine-checkable callable, pre/postcondition and effect contracts.

GAP-016.reason: ANIL provides a real localized task-to-head parameter transformation, but not low-rank adaptation, independent-delta composition or a weight-space function algebra.

GAP-017.reason: Accuracy/return proximity and CCA/CKA similarity do not constitute a checker for semantic or behavioral equivalence across MAML, ANIL, NIL or other carriers.

GAP-018.reason: RL trajectories and mutable training state expose an application domain but no language-level effects, handlers, authority, transaction or rollback semantics.

GAP-019.reason: The paper distinguishes shared and task-specific parameters but supplies no method release or versioned provenance/compatibility/rollback registry.

GAP-020.reason: Task distributions, stochastic policies and run variability are explicit, but the method has no calibrated probabilistic function semantics or governed uncertainty interface.

source_specific_reasoning: PARTIAL is the evidence-corrected result. The exact paper directly confirms a reusable-body/task-specific-head representation and a bounded task-to-head adaptation operator, with carefully scoped benchmark evidence that body feature reuse dominates in the tested MAML configurations. It does not confirm the historical card's low-rank adapter, task-description input, weight-delta checkpoint, stateless adapter runtime or adapter arithmetic/routing template. Three-seed point estimates, CCA/CKA similarity and baseline repositories do not establish equivalence or independent reproduction.
confirmed_projection: The exact ICLR paper confirms a bounded neural Representation and partial Compiler/Artifact pattern: meta-training can learn a reusable feature body while support-data gradients produce an ephemeral task-specific head, and a cosine classifier can reuse body features directly on the tested few-shot classification distributions. This is evidence for localized neural adaptation, not for low-rank adapters, arbitrary function compilation, weight algebra, routing or a governed runtime.
projection_boundary: These are 121CX projections from the exact registered 21-page arXiv v2 paper, every rendered page, complete TeX source and audited current states of both paper-linked baseline repositories. ANIL/NIL experiments were not rerun and no author-specific implementation or paper-run receipt was available. This model review is not a proof, statistical equivalence test, independent replication, empirical validation of the reported results, or validation of ignition.
what_the_paper_does_not_support: It does not define or evaluate LoRA, low-rank matrices, adapter modules or compact delta checkpoints.
It does not map a natural-language task description to a parameter delta; adaptation consumes labelled support examples or trajectories and a loss.
It does not compose, add, interpolate, merge or route among independently learned adapters or callable functions.
It does not prove that MAML always performs feature reuse or that body adaptation is unnecessary outside the evaluated architectures and task distributions.
It does not establish semantic, functional or statistical equivalence between MAML, ANIL or NIL.
High CCA/CKA similarity does not prove identical input-output behavior or substitutability on all inputs.
It does not turn an ordinary neural forward pass into a function-language interpreter.
It does not define external effect contracts, capabilities, execution traces or a versioned function registry.
It does not release an author-certified ANIL/NIL implementation or provenance-complete experiment artifact.
This review does not independently validate the paper's reported accuracy, return or speedup.
limitations_and_failure_boundaries: The central feature-reuse conclusion is empirical and scoped mainly to shallow four-layer convolutional MAML models on Omniglot and MiniImageNet, plus three simulated RL tasks.
Freezing all body layers reduces reported MiniImageNet 5-shot accuracy by 2.1 points; describing the change as negligible is a judgment, not a formal equivalence result.
Only three training initializations are used, with no seed IDs, raw values, confidence intervals, paired tests, effect sizes or predeclared equivalence margins.
MAML and ANIL point estimates are not uniformly close: ANIL is much higher on HalfCheetah-Direction and lower on MiniImageNet 5-shot, among other differences.
Representation similarity metrics have invariances and input-sampling dependence; they do not certify semantic identity.
The paper's CCA language sometimes moves from high similarity to little functional change, which remains an inference supported by freezing results rather than a proof.
Euclidean parameter distance is explicitly acknowledged as a weaker proxy for functional change.
Appendix A describes MiniImageNet test-time tasks as using validation classes despite separately listing 24 test classes, leaving the exact evaluation split textually ambiguous.
The RL MAML results do not reproduce the original paper's numbers, and the authors attribute this in part to large initialization variance.
RL selects the best model over 500 training iterations before test-task evaluation without a separately specified validation-selection protocol.
ANIL still differentiates through adapted head parameters and retains second-order terms; it is not equivalent to first-order MAML.
NIL depends on a meta-trained representation and labelled support examples; no-inner-loop does not mean task-free or data-free inference.
Timing excludes data loading and uses one TensorFlow graph, one Titan-Xp, batch/target size 1 and 2,000 batches; speedups may not transfer to other frameworks, devices or workloads.
The TeX package contains figures and prose but no ANIL/NIL code, exact seeds, checkpoints, raw metrics, timing logs or environment lock.
The linked cbfinn/maml and tristandeleu/pytorch-maml-rl repositories implement baseline MAML and contain no identifiable ANIL/NIL modification.
Current repository heads are mutable states and cannot be assumed to be the exact dependency revisions used for the paper.
No distribution-shift, adversarial, calibration, safety, real-world effects, long-horizon lifecycle or cross-version compatibility evaluation is reported.
This audit verifies the paper package and public artifact boundary but does not execute the legacy TensorFlow/PyTorch experiments.

corrections: Replaced the metadata-only 2019/preprint framing with the exact arXiv v2 and ICLR 2020 published-paper identity.
Reviewed all 21 pages, complete TeX source and both paper-linked baseline repository states rather than projecting from the title.
Rejected the prior function definition 'incremental parameter delta' and replaced it with a reusable body plus dense task-adapted head and NIL support-representation carrier.
Rejected the invented task-description input and low-rank-weight-delta output; the actual inner loop consumes support data/trajectories and updates the full dense head.
Rejected adapter parameters, base-model-plus-adapter runtime and adapter arithmetic/routing because none appears in the paper.
Confirmed a bounded task-to-head gradient generator and body feature-reuse result while preserving the lack of formal callable contracts and semantic guarantees.
Separated CCA/CKA representation similarity, benchmark-performance proximity and freezing ablations from semantic or statistical equivalence.
Recorded three-seed statistics, RL best-iterate selection, mismatched original-MAML RL results, single-device timing scope and MiniImageNet split wording ambiguity.
Separated baseline MAML repositories from a missing author-specific ANIL/NIL release and paper-run receipt.
Did not call equations proof, point-estimate similarity equivalence, public baseline code reproduction, or this model review validation of ignition.

paper_core_claims.claim: DARE constructs a sparse task delta by randomly dropping delta parameters and rescaling retained entries by 1/(1-p), then applies an existing model-merging operator to the processed same-base deltas.
For one affine layer with a fixed input and independent Bernoulli mask, rescaling makes the masked layer output equal to the original fine-tuned layer output in expectation.
On the selected encoder and decoder benchmarks, DARE preprocessing often improves existing merging methods and can tolerate high drop rates when fine-tuning deltas are small.
Compatibility with the same pretrained base is operationally critical; using an incorrect base or directly dropping fine-tuned weights can collapse performance.
The paper's open-ended merger examples are weight-space capability combinations, not guarantees of equivalence, monotonic improvement or safe behavior.

function_concept_used_by_paper: A model is represented as a pretrained base parameter vector plus a task-specific fine-tuning delta. DARE stochastically sparsifies and rescales each delta, after which a compatible merging rule such as Task Arithmetic, averaging, Fisher, RegMean or TIES produces one combined parameter vector. This directly instantiates bounded weight-space function composition among homologous same-architecture, same-base neural models; it is not activation-level fine-tuning, arbitrary callable composition or semantic equivalence.
specification_language: The merge recipe comprises exact base/source checkpoint identities, task deltas, drop probability p, rescaling choice, merge method and method-specific coefficients. This is an operational numerical recipe, not a typed FunctionSpec with named input/output schemas, preconditions, effects, authority, failure semantics, resource budgets or lifecycle policy.

representation_or_carrier.source_carrier: fine-tuned checkpoint theta_SFT^t and derived task delta delta^t = theta_SFT^t - theta_PRE
representation_or_carrier.dare_carrier: Bernoulli mask plus sparse rescaled task delta hat_delta^t
representation_or_carrier.composed_carrier: one merged parameter vector theta_M with the same architecture and tensor shapes
representation_or_carrier.compatibility_boundary: The evaluated source models are homologous derivatives of one base. Same shape alone is insufficient when the actual originating base differs.

compiler_or_generator.dare_transform: Sample an elementwise Bernoulli drop mask, zero selected delta entries and divide retained entries by 1-p.
compiler_or_generator.merge_transform: Feed processed deltas/checkpoints to an existing arithmetic merger and materialize one merged checkpoint.
compiler_or_generator.classification: This is a concrete artifact generator and weight-space lowering pipeline, but only a partial compiler analogy because the input intent is not a declarative callable contract and no semantic-preservation theorem is supplied.

interpreter_or_runtime: The merged checkpoint executes through its ordinary transformer forward pass and decoding/evaluation stack. The paper defines no function bytecode, evaluator for independently represented callable functions, effect handler, capability runtime, exception contract or general Function OS interpreter.
state_or_effect_model: Merging reads and writes large parameter tensors; inference maintains ordinary model/cache state. Benchmarks exercise text generation and classification, but the method gives no language-level effect signatures, authority, transactions, idempotence, compensation, rollback or external-action safety semantics.
composition_rule: For Task Arithmetic, theta_M = theta_PRE + lambda times the sum of DARE-processed task deltas. Other evaluated methods substitute their own averaging, Fisher, RegMean or TIES rule after the same masking preprocessing. Composition is restricted to architecture-compatible homologous checkpoints and is not closed over arbitrary functions.

equivalence_notions.support: The paper derives equality in expectation for a single affine layer under independent random masking and fixed input.
equivalence_notions.boundary: This does not prove equality for an individual mask, nonlinear multilayer outputs, embeddings, task behavior or merged-model semantics. The omitted elementwise delta variance is p/(1-p) times delta squared and grows sharply as p approaches 1.

equivalence_notions.support: Source, dropped and merged models are compared on GLUE, AlpacaEval, GSM8K, MATH, HumanEval and MBPP point metrics.
equivalence_notions.boundary: No equivalence margin, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence interval or significance test is supplied, and metrics trade off across DARE settings.

equivalence_notions.support: A merged model can score on several source-task benchmarks after weight arithmetic.
equivalence_notions.boundary: This is a finite benchmark observation, not proof that source functions are preserved, combined without interference or equivalent to an ensemble or joint training.

validation_regime.formal: The paper provides definitions and a limited expected-output calculation for one affine layer. It gives no theorem for end-to-end functional equivalence, semantic preservation, convergence, generalization, interference bounds or safety.
validation_regime.encoder: Fine-tuned RoBERTa-base models are merged across GLUE tasks. The original train split is divided 90/10 for training/validation and original GLUE validation is called test. The released script then grid-searches merge and DARE hyperparameters directly on that reported test dataset, so the headline encoder results are selection-contaminated.
validation_regime.decoder: WizardLM-13B, WizardMath-13B and llama-2-13b-code-alpaca are merged from the Llama2-13B base and evaluated by greedy decoding on instruction, math and code benchmarks. Results are point estimates; no seed/run count, error bar, confidence interval or statistical test is given.
validation_regime.tradeoffs: DARE is not uniformly dominant. For three-model TIES it raises AlpacaEval 65.91 to 72.50 and HumanEval 21.95 to 29.27 while GSM8K falls 62.55 to 58.00 and MATH 9.54 to 9.20. Other rows likewise mix gains and losses.
validation_regime.failure_cases: WizardCoder-Python-13B evaluated against Llama2 rather than its CodeLlama base falls from 63.41/55.4 on HumanEval/MBPP to 0/0 after only 10 percent delta dropping. Directly dropping fine-tuned weights also collapses at low rates. WizardLM-70B on AlpacaEval is not robust to every high drop rate.
validation_regime.leaderboard_boundary: The supermario_v2 Open LLM leaderboard rank is explicitly time-bounded to January 28, 2024; the comparison is dynamic and one listed source model lacks a directly reported row in the paper table.
validation_regime.hardware: Experiments used V100/A100 GPUs. The code README says decoder merging requires GPU memory proportional to number of models times tensor parallel size, so no-retraining/no-extra-training must not be rewritten as a GPU-free full workflow.
validation_regime.artifact: Official code exposes the method and grids but lacks a license, tests, CI, environment lock, exact dependency versions, raw logs, checkpoints and result receipts. Syntax review is not experimental reproduction.
validation_regime.safety: No safety, bias, privacy, adversarial, robustness-under-shift or external-action evaluation is reported; the impact statement acknowledges source harms may persist.

uncertainty_model: DARE explicitly samples independent Bernoulli masks and reasons about one-layer expectation, but does not report mask seeds, repeated-mask dispersion or variance. The retained delta estimator has elementwise variance p/(1-p) times delta squared under the stated mask, which the paper does not propagate through nonlinear layers or benchmark metrics. Experimental tables are uncalibrated point estimates without run counts, error bars, confidence intervals or selection-adjusted uncertainty; released code fixes random seed 0.
lifecycle_and_provenance: The method requires a named pretrained base, compatible fine-tuned source checkpoints, derived deltas, mask/drop settings, merge method/coefficient and a materialized merged checkpoint. This is useful lineage structure, but the paper/repository provide no immutable manifest binding each reported number to source hashes, code commit, environment, mask seed and evaluation receipt. There is no governed compatibility registry, approval, rollout monitoring, deprecation, migration or rollback protocol. The frozen S120-082 binding itself demonstrates why identity and hash-to-semantics checks are mandatory.

N1_FunctionSpec.reason: Base/source identities and a numerical merge recipe specify a bounded operation, but not a typed callable contract with pre/postconditions and effects.

N2_Representation.reason: Base checkpoint, task deltas, masks and the merged vector are explicit weight-space neural-function carriers.

N3_Compiler.reason: DARE plus a merge operator concretely generates a merged artifact, but it does not lower a declarative function specification or guarantee semantic preservation.

N4_Artifact.reason: Source and merged checkpoints are concrete artifacts, while immutable paper-run hashes, environments, mask seeds and evaluation receipts are missing.

N5_Interpreter.reason: An ordinary transformer forward pass is not an interpreter for independently represented functions or a function language.

N6_ExecutionTrace.reason: Aggregate benchmark outputs and merge logs do not define a replayable per-execution trace schema.

N7_Validator.reason: Multiple benchmarks and ablations provide bounded empirical checks, but encoder test-set tuning, point-only results and absent safety/equivalence tests sharply limit validation.

N8_ComposerRouter.reason: DARE preprocessing plus Task Arithmetic and related merge operators is genuine bounded weight-space composition of homologous models; it is not a runtime router.

N9_VersionedRegistry.reason: Base/source/merged identities and recipes are necessary registry fields, but no immutable compatibility, lineage, rollout or rollback registry is implemented.

GAP-015.reason: The merge recipe is machine-operational but lacks typed callable, effect and lifecycle contracts.

GAP-016.reason: The paper directly defines same-base neural weight deltas and arithmetic composition, with explicit compatibility and interference boundaries.

GAP-017.reason: One-layer expectation and finite benchmark scores are not semantic, behavioral or statistical equivalence checkers.

GAP-018.reason: Tensor mutation and inference do not supply language-level effects, authority, transactions or rollback semantics.

GAP-019.reason: Base/source/merged checkpoint lineage and merge recipes are direct provenance fragments, but immutable receipts, compatibility policy and governed rollback are absent.

GAP-020.reason: Bernoulli masking and expected affine output are explicit stochastic elements, but variance is not propagated or calibrated and experiments lack uncertainty reporting.

source_specific_reasoning: CONFIRMED is bounded to the uniquely recovered intended ICML paper, not to the frozen wrong PDF or invented frozen title. The exact frozen bytes are an unrelated quantum-amplifier paper and receive zero semantic credit. The intended paper directly confirms homologous-model weight deltas and weight-space composition, including concrete DARE masking/rescaling before established merge operators. Confirmation does not extend to arbitrary functions, activation-level alignment, equivalence, uniform improvement, GPU-free execution, safe deployment or provenance-complete reproduction.
confirmed_projection: The recovered published DARE paper confirms N2 Representation and N8 ComposerRouter for a narrow but genuine case: architecture-compatible models derived from the same base can be represented as task deltas, stochastically transformed and combined by weight arithmetic into one executable checkpoint. It also exposes base identity, tensor compatibility, interference, stochastic variance and immutable provenance as first-class Function OS constraints.
projection_boundary: These are 121CX projections from the exact frozen 8-page wrong-binding PDF, every rendered page of the recovered 21-page official paper, complete arXiv v3 source and audited current official repository. Experiments were not rerun. This model review is not a proof, statistical equivalence test, independent replication, empirical validation of reported results, validation of ignition, or authority to repair frozen registries.
what_the_paper_does_not_support: The frozen title 'DARE: Language Model Alignment via Activation Level Fine-tuning' and arXiv:2402.12045 do not identify this method; that PDF is unrelated quantum physics.
DARE does not fine-tune or align activations; it drops and rescales elements of weight deltas before model merging.
It does not compose arbitrary architectures, arbitrary callable functions or checkpoints with different originating bases.
It does not prove that a sampled sparse delta, final embedding, output distribution or merged behavior equals the source model.
It does not establish uniform metric improvement, non-interference, ensemble equivalence or joint-training equivalence.
It does not define a typed FunctionSpec, external effect/capability model, execution-trace contract or general interpreter.
It does not provide calibrated uncertainty, repeated-mask confidence intervals or statistical tests.
It does not validate safety, bias, privacy, adversarial robustness or downstream external actions.
It does not provide a provenance-complete, licensed, immutable reproduction package for the reported results.
This review does not independently validate the paper's benchmark numbers or claims.
limitations_and_failure_boundaries: The frozen registry is bibliographically corrupted: title, identifier and exact bytes point to different works. Semantic recovery rests on the remaining author/year/method/function metadata and is recorded rather than silently repairing frozen files.
DARE requires homologous same-shape models derived from the same pretrained base; a wrong-base example collapses to zero code benchmark scores after a small drop rate.
The single-affine-layer expectation argument assumes an independent mask and fixed input; it is not an end-to-end nonlinear-network theorem.
Per-element estimator variance p/(1-p) times delta squared diverges as p approaches 1, while the paper reports no variance propagation or repeated-mask dispersion.
High drop tolerance depends on small fine-tuning deltas and task/model particulars; even a 70B instruction model is not uniformly robust at high rates.
Directly masking fine-tuned weights rather than base-relative deltas causes severe failure, so representation choice is essential.
Main tables contain metric tradeoffs; DARE often helps selected objectives but can reduce math, instruction or code metrics in the same merge.
Encoder hyperparameters are selected on the same original GLUE validation split reported as test, contaminating model selection and evaluation.
No experiment seeds, run counts, error bars, confidence intervals, statistical tests or selection-adjusted uncertainty are reported; code uses a fixed seed 0.
Decoder evaluation uses greedy decoding and finite benchmark samples; no distribution-shift, prompt-sensitivity or contamination analysis is supplied.
The leaderboard rank is a dated snapshot, not a stable property, and source-model comparison is incomplete in the corresponding table.
The no-GPU rhetoric applies at most to no additional training/arithmetic concept; the paper used V100/A100 hardware and the README requires substantial GPU memory for its decoder workflow.
The repository has no LICENSE, tags, tests, CI, environment lock, raw logs, checkpoints or immutable result receipts, and includes author-machine paths.
The audited repository head predates arXiv v3 and cannot be assumed to be the exact camera-ready experiment state.
No safety or harmful-capability evaluation is reported; model merging can preserve or combine undesirable source behavior.

corrections: Recorded that exact frozen arXiv:2402.12045 is Broadband parametric amplification in DARTWARS and supplies no model-merging evidence.

Recovered the intended Le Yu et al. ICML 2024 paper from the jointly unique author/year/DARE/weight-arithmetic metadata without rewriting frozen registries.
Reviewed all pages and source of both the wrong frozen binding and intended published paper, plus the official repository implementation/history.
Confirmed base-relative deltas, Bernoulli drop/rescale and bounded homologous-model weight composition.
Replaced an unqualified deterministic label with the actual stochastic mask, one-layer expectation and unreported variance boundary.
Separated merge performance from semantic/equivalence claims and recorded non-uniform metric tradeoffs and catastrophic wrong-base failure.
Exposed reported-test-set hyperparameter selection in the released GLUE code and absence of run-level uncertainty.
Separated no additional training from the GPU/memory needs of the published implementation and evaluation workflow.
